issues.author: lukedhlee
issues.body:
I evaluated the Snowball R2E-Gym RL checkpoints under [Eval Policy v0.1](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9193) (harbor `7b18505a`, the recovery job files from `8aa9a354`, one trial per task, 16 concurrent, 32,768 / 8,192 tokens, terminus-2 defaults, Daytona). Two things came out that I think matter beyond Snowball. Full write-up with the training-side story: https://gist.github.com/lukedhlee/01897efa3ae7c474732c61d35150a43a (Part III).

**Checkpoints.** Base = [laion/snowball-67b-a2b-sft-s3-nemotron-terminal-step1888](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-sft-s3-nemotron-terminal-step1888). RL = GRPO on R2E-Gym repository-fix tasks with terminus-2 (terminal only), [old stack update 36](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-rl-r2egym-oldstack-step36) and [new stack update 24](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-rl-r2egym-newstack-step24), the pick. Two later checkpoints are in the figure too: [update 48](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-rl-r2egym-newstack-step48) of the same run, and update 24 continued for 24 more updates on a refreshed pool of 1,247 tasks. Training ran terminus-2 with summarization **off** at 49,152 input / 16,384 output tokens.

### 1. The RL gain is in-distribution: SWE-bench Verified moves, Terminal-Bench 2 does not

![Under Marin's eval policy, the RL gain shows on SWE-bench and not on Terminal-Bench 2](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/lukedhlee/f50158cdcffb2a6367d26f63432a3f2a/raw/3998f0fb24fe70f1d6aa7d55fa575b2255bc51e9/fig5_policy_id_vs_ood.png)

Whiskers are 95% intervals, about ±8 points with one trial per task. Paired on SWE-bench the new checkpoint solves 15 tasks the base does not and loses 4 (12 to 8 against the old stack). On TB2 the base and the two RL picks are within noise and update 24 is lowest in every setting I tried. Training longer does not move SWE-bench: update 48 scores 25 against update 24's 23 and wins 13 tasks while losing 11, the same churn two identical runs of update 24 show (23 and 24, disagreeing on 22 tasks). The refreshed pool did not buy transfer: 17 on SWE-bench, losing 16 tasks to update 24 and winning 10, and 5 of 89 on TB2. The one hint of anything is update 48 on TB2, 9 of 87 against 4, winning 6 and losing 1, still inside a one-trial interval. TB2 denominators are scored tasks; 0 to 4 trials per run were lost to infrastructure (mostly the agent running `pkill -f` inside the sandbox, which kills harbor's own tmux command), inside the 10 % allowance, and counting them as failures does not change the order.

R2E-Gym and SWE-bench are the same kind of work, a Python repo with failing tests to fix, and that is where the 11 points show up. The RL checkpoint declares done fast (median 4 minutes of agent time per SWE-bench task vs 21 for the base), which is what finishing inside the window looks like on repo fixes and what giving up early looks like on TB2's long build-and-verify tasks.

### 2. Summarization helps the RL checkpoint, even though it was never trained with it

SWE-bench random-100 at the policy setting, at 32k with summarization off, and at the training setting (49k/16k, off), for base and the new checkpoint:

![How each SWE-bench trial ended, by terminus-2 setting](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/lukedhlee/f50158cdcffb2a6367d26f63432a3f2a/raw/cac4e15e3f7d8f684aa35b7bddb24ec58bdd5042/fig6_summarization_context.png)

All 600 trials scored, no infrastructure losses. A trial that runs out of context stops and is graded as it stands. Caveat: the base's two summarization-off rows were served at temperature 0.7 with a repetition penalty of 1.1 by mistake; every other row is temperature 1.0 with no penalty. It cannot change the picture for a model that overflows on 97 of 100 tasks, but those two rows are not sampler-paired with the rest. Agent requests in all runs set `skip_special_tokens: false` so the think markers stay in the transcript; Marin's agentic launcher does not set this flag today. A paired probe says it does not matter for the score: the RL checkpoint at the policy setting scores 23 and 24 of 100 with the flag (two runs) and 23 without it, and the two flag-on runs disagree on as many tasks (22) as flag-on vs flag-off (23), so per-task differences are sampling noise at temperature 1.0.

- The base cannot work without summarization: 94 to 97 of 100 trials overflow at either budget. RL cut that to 42 at the training budget.
- The RL checkpoint's best number is with summarization on, which training never used, and its lead over base is the same size in every setting (+11, +5, +11). RL improved the task skill rather than fitting one context regime.
- Summarization at 32k beats a 49k window without it, for both models. 23 vs 19 is inside the one-trial noise; a 3-trial rerun (~15 GH200 node-hours) would settle it.

**Takeaways for the policy.** Keeping terminus-2's summarization on in v0.1 is the right call for this model family, and it is not a mismatch with how the checkpoint was trained. SWE-bench random-100 is the ID leg that detects R2E-Gym RL; TB2 does not, at this checkpoint.

**Reproduction.** Stack, task revisions (DCAgent2/terminal_bench_2, DCAgent2/swebench-verified-random-100-folders `0c553bd6`) and the variant configs are in the gist's "Policy evaluation" section. Job directories and traces are on JSC Jupiter; happy to attach any trial.

# Research

Goal (from sibling issues #6603/#6605/#6658): run **OLMoBaseEval Easy** inside Marin so checkpoints don't have to egress to SC for evals ("so we don't need SC transfer"). "Flagging missing evals" means comparing the OLMoBaseEval Easy task set against Marin's eval configs and listing the gaps.

Two distinct gaps matter, not just task names:
- **Coverage** — which Table 9 tasks have no `EvalTaskConfig` in Marin.
- **Formatting** — Marin runs Eleuther **LM Eval Harness with default prompts**; OLMoBaseEval is **OLMES**-formatted. `marin-32b-retro.md` explicitly notes results diverge from OLMES due to prompt/format. So a task present by *name* (e.g. `arc_easy`, `hellaswag`, `social_iqa`) is **not** the OLMoBaseEval version — name-matching alone would mis-flag coverage as complete.

**Relevant code**
- [`experiments/evals/task_configs.py#L11-L27`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/task_configs.py#L11-L27) — `CORE_TASKS` (OLMES-style core MCQ already present by name)
- [`experiments/evals/task_configs.py#L538-L556`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/task_configs.py#L538-L556) — `convert_to_task_metrics`
- [`experiments/evals/evals.py#L43`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/evals.py#L43) — LM-Eval-Harness runner (default prompts)

# Blocker / what I need

I can't authoritatively flag gaps without the canonical list. Web access is disabled in my environment and "Olmix Table 9" / OLMoBaseEval Easy isn't in the repo. Please provide:

1. **Table 9 contents** — the OLMoBaseEval Easy task list, ideally with per-task **num_fewshot**, **metric**, and **format/normalization** (OLMES MC vs cloze, length-norm, etc.). A link to the Olmix doc/paper or a paste both work.

comments.author: Calvin-Xu
comments.body:
🤖 Update: Fieldbook tracking started and CC planning review completed.

Fieldbook experiment:
- `exp_01kw0hpzfm2besk662a4g8nmyh` — `Issue 6665: Reliability-weighted OLMoBaseEval modeling`

Baseline being improved:
- Effective-exposure DSP on the OLMoBaseEval Easy paper-style Table-9 macro.
- Target: `table9_macro_bpb = mean_51_table9_bpb_components`, lower is better.
- Current best baseline: OOF Spearman `0.918`, OOF RMSE `0.01284`, regret@1 `0.00739`, lower-tail optimism `0.00696`.
- Baseline artifact: `experiments/domain_phase_mix/exploratory/two_phase_many/reference_outputs/olmo_base_easy_table9_macro_dsp_300m_20260625/effective_exposure_table9_macro_fit_summary.csv`

Reliability source:
- Domain-deletion p-value/t-stat matrix from 39 leave-one-domain-out ablations calibrated against 11 proportional-reference observations.
- Artifact: `experiments/domain_phase_mix/exploratory/two_phase_many/reference_outputs/olmo_base_easy_domain_ablation_pvalue_matrix_20260625/smooth_benchmark_deleted_domain_pvalue_matrix_cells.csv`
- Fit panel: `experiments/domain_phase_mix/exploratory/two_phase_many/reference_outputs/olmo_base_easy_paper_faithful_olmix_300m_20260625/fit_panel_table9_macro.csv`

CC review result: `experiments/domain_phase_mix/exploratory/two_phase_many/reference_outputs/olmo_base_easy_reliability_weighting_20260625/cc_planning_review_20260625.md`

Main changes to the plan after CC review:

1. Keep the headline estimand fixed: the unweighted 51-component Table-9 macro BPB. Reliability-weighted targets are allowed only as exploratory diagnostics, not the main objective.
2. Add an inverse-variance-only control using proportional repeat noise. If inverse-variance weighting matches reliability weighting, the 39-domain deletion matrix is not adding useful information.
3. Avoid label leakage from global reliability weights. Either recompute the deletion-effect numerator inside each training fold or explicitly report global-vs-fold-local optimism.
4. Build an explicit crosswalk from the p-value matrix components to the 51 Table-9 macro components, especially MMLU grouping and ARC.
5. Report qsplit/signal-row and deletion-row OOF metrics separately, because deletion rows are high-leverage extrapolation points.
6. Require decision-relevant improvements: regret@1, lower-tail RMSE/optimism, and top-k predicted observed rows. Spearman-only gains are not enough to justify a mixture submission.

Planned analysis matrix:

- `single_macro_unweighted`: current Effective-exposure DSP baseline.
- `single_macro_reliability_weighted`: one macro fit using continuous reliability information, evaluated on the unweighted macro.
- `per_component_unweighted`: fit one model per Table-9 component, aggregate predictions uniformly.
- `per_component_reliability_weighted`: per-component fits with reliability-aware fitting/aggregation, still evaluated against the unweighted macro.

Required controls/diagnostics before proposing any optimized mixture:

- Noise floor: SD of the 11 proportional-reference macro BPBs versus current OOF RMSE.
- Reliability weights versus inverse-variance weights.
- Reliability weights versus per-component OOF predictability.
- Per-component OOF R² histogram.
- Global versus fold-local reliability weighting.
- Permuted-reliability null distribution.
- Top-1/top-5 predicted observed rows by method.
- Metrics split by qsplit/signal rows versus deletion rows.

Decision rule: do not submit a reliability-weighted optimized mixture unless it improves the fixed unweighted macro objective over current Effective-exposure DSP and clears the inverse-variance and permuted-reliability controls.

comments.author: Calvin-Xu
comments.body:
🤖 First-pass reliability-weighted target sweep is complete.

Artifacts:
- Script: `experiments/domain_phase_mix/exploratory/two_phase_many/analyze_olmo_base_easy_reliability_weighting_300m.py`
- Output dir: `experiments/domain_phase_mix/exploratory/two_phase_many/reference_outputs/olmo_base_easy_reliability_weighting_20260625/`
- Summary: `method_summary.csv`
- Report: `report.md`
- Plots: `component_reliability_diagnostics.html`, `lambda_sweep_headline_metrics.html`, `best_reliability_variant_oof_scatter.html`

Setup:
- Target panel: 280 rows = 241 qsplit/signal + 39 domain deletion rows.
- Components: 51 OLMoBaseEval Easy Table-9 BPB components.
- Reliability source: domain-deletion p-value matrix calibrated against 11 proportional references.
- DSP: Effective-exposure, fixed `LINEAR_REG=1e-4` for this first pass.
- Tried reliability statistics: one-sided harm `t`-excess, two-sided `t`-excess, one-/two-sided Bonferroni min-p, and inverse variance.
- Lambda grid: `{0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1}`.
- Evaluation remains the unweighted 51-component Table-9 macro BPB.

Main result: target reweighting is negative so far. The uniform unweighted macro remains best.

| method | lambda | OOF Spearman | OOF RMSE | regret@1 | lower-tail optimism | predicted best |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| uniform | 0.00 | 0.9200 | 0.012690 | 0.007388 | 0.007008 | `run_00056` |
| two_sided_t_excess | 0.25 | 0.9079 | 0.021174 | 0.007388 | 0.019446 | `run_00056` |
| harm_t_excess | 0.25 | 0.9107 | 0.024032 | 0.007388 | 0.023484 | `run_00056` |
| harm_bonferroni | 0.25 | 0.9074 | 0.025949 | 0.007388 | 0.025443 | `run_00056` |
| inverse_variance | 0.25 | 0.9073 | 0.034710 | 0.007388 | 0.032423 | `run_00056` |

Interpretation:
- The p-value matrix has strong signal, but using it as aggregate target weights changes the estimand and worsens prediction of the unweighted Table-9 macro.
- The inverse-variance-only control also worsens, so this is not just “noisy components should be downweighted.”
- The next thing to test is not more aggressive target weighting. Instead, reliability should probably enter as a precision/selection diagnostic, as row/intervention weighting, or in a per-component modeling setup where the headline objective remains the unweighted macro.

Next planned variants:
- Per-component Effective-exposure DSP fits, then aggregate predictions uniformly and with reliability only as a diagnostic/secondary selector.
- Fold-local reliability sensitivity to check global-reliability leakage.
- Row/intervention weighting, if we can implement it without changing the DSP estimand.

comments.author: Calvin-Xu
comments.body:
🤖 Follow-up after CC review and local verification of the first-pass reliability-weighted target result.

Important correction to interpretation: the previous target-weighting sweep should not be read as “reliability weighting is harmful.” The main degradation in headline RMSE is an estimand-shift artifact:

- Uniform fits and evaluates the same target, so `weighted_target_oof_rmse == headline_oof_rmse == 0.012690`.
- Inverse-variance `lambda=1` fits its own weighted target better (`weighted_target_oof_rmse = 0.009980`) than uniform, but scores badly against the unweighted macro (`headline_oof_rmse = 0.128957`).
- That means the weighting is changing the objective, not necessarily making the model worse.
- Selection is saturated: most methods still choose `run_00056`, while the best observed row is `run_00018`.

Local panel sanity check:

- qsplit/signal rows: `241`
- unique qsplit run names: `241`
- unique qsplit weight vectors: `241`
- domain-deletion rows: `39`

So the immediate problem is not duplicate qsplit mixtures. The remaining concern is that random-row OOF metrics may be dominated by easy boundary deletion contrasts, not by the hard near-optimal interior ranking problem.

Revised approach:

1. Stop treating aggregate target reweighting as the main route. It changes the estimand away from the unweighted Table-9 macro.
2. Move to one Effective-exposure DSP per Table-9 component, then aggregate predictions as the unweighted macro: `M_hat(w) = (1/51) sum_c g_c(w)`.
3. Use reliability for shrinkage / precision / secondary diagnostics rather than changing the final target weights.
4. Re-score with grouped and stratified CV: full panel, qsplit-only/interior rows, and deletion rows separately.
5. Use selection-centric criteria: regret@1/@3, top-k observed quality, lower-tail optimism, and whether the model fixes the current `run_00056` vs `run_00018` miss.
6. Recompute MMLU category reliability from direct 11-repeat category aggregates, not leaf-independence variance reconstruction.

Next planned artifact: a per-component Effective-exposure DSP harness that compares aggregate DSP, paper-faithful OLMix, and per-component DSP under identical grouped/stratified OOF scoring.

comments.author: Calvin-Xu
comments.body:
🤖 Per-component uncertainty-aware DSP decision diagnostic is now implemented and logged in Fieldbook.

What this run tests:
- Headline target remains the unweighted OLMoBaseEval Easy Table-9 macro BPB.
- Reliability is used as uncertainty / guardrail evidence, not as a replacement objective.
- Per-component Effective-exposure DSP is compared against the current aggregate Effective-exposure DSP and paper-faithful OLMix baselines.
- Decision metrics include OOF RMSE/Spearman, fold Regret@1/3/5, full Regret@1/3/5, post-selection optimism, selected actual rank, and component guardrail violations.

Important caveat on the OOF convention:
- This is not a fully nested nonlinear refit for every fold. It uses full-data nonlinear DSP geometry and fold-refit linear heads. That is intentional for a first decision screen; full nested refits should only be paid for if this cheaper diagnostic shows a plausible improvement.

Main result:
- This first per-component pass is negative relative to aggregate DSP.
- Best qsplit selector remains `aggregate_dsp_effective_exposure_0p0001`: OOF Spearman `0.914`, OOF RMSE `0.0136`, selected run `run_00056`, selected actual rank `2`.

- The per-component harness is useful diagnostically, but it does not yet improve selection over the aggregate DSP baseline.

Worst component fits in this pass include `basic_skills_logical_reasoning`, `csqa`, `basic_skills_common_knowledge`, `basic_skills_pattern`, and `arc_challenge`. Next work should focus on why those components are poorly modeled, qsplit-only vs deletion-augmented training behavior, and whether reliability should enter as fold-local uncertainty / guardrails rather than target reweighting.

## Description
Expand `experiments/evals/ppl_circuit_coverage_v2.py` with small, reviewable circuit/task families for issue #6070. These probes should test basic code-interpretation functionality with compact few-shot ICL, target-only supervised validation, and plain-text training documents.

Workflow for a contributor:

1. Pick one small task or family.
2. Add a `PplCircuitCoverageV2Family` value if needed, add slices to `PPL_CIRCUIT_COVERAGE_V2_SLICES`, implement `_generate_<task>`, and register it in `_GENERATORS`.
3. Keep prompts compact: completed few-shot lines followed by one completion prefix. Do not add `Family:`, `Task:`, `Prompt:`, `worked examples`, `held-out query`, `answer:`, or `Final answer:`.
4. Return supervised rows with `input` ending before the held-out answer and `output` containing only the final answer plus newline.
5. Generate a small local sample:
   `uv run python -c 'from experiments.evals.ppl_circuit_coverage_v2 import write_local_sample; write_local_sample("/tmp/ppl_circuit_v2_sample", examples_per_config=36)'`
6. Inspect the plain-text ICL examples manually for ambiguity, leakage, and broken escaping.
7. Run validation tests:
   `uv run --with pytest --with pytest-timeout pytest -m "not slow" tests/evals/test_ppl_circuit_coverage_v2.py -q`
8. Confirm the plain-text training renderer still produces `input + output`, and that the raw validation split uses supervised `input`/`output` target-only scoring.

Good first task candidates:

- String parsing: split/join, prefix/suffix trimming, delimiter extraction, balanced quote parsing.
- Structured data: JSONPath-lite lookup, nested Python literal lookup, CSV quoting/escaping.
- Arithmetic: integer division/remainder, bitwise ops, small rational simplification, date arithmetic.
- Code semantics: boolean expression evaluation, operator precedence, small loop trace, function-call argument binding.
- Text formatting: indentation normalization, bullet renumbering, fixed-width alignment.
- State machines: URL/path normalization, simple lexer tokenization, calculator stack traces.

### Definition of Done
- One new task or tightly related family is added to the v2 generator and registry.
- Generated local samples include at least 36 examples for the new task and look correct on manual inspection.
- Tests verify the target from metadata and enforce compact target-only supervised formatting.

Three task generators, each ~50 lines plus shared helpers and tests — total expected diff ~350-450 lines plus five generated example snippets in the PR body, which exceeds the 100-line auto-PR threshold and is a new feature, so I am holding for review rather than pushing.

Proposed slices:
1. `bool_expr_eval` — short Python-like boolean expression over named ints/bools (`(a < b) and not c` with `a=2, b=5, c=False`), target is the literal `True`/`False`.

Each generator follows the existing recipe: two completed few-shot lines via `_few_shot_block`, one completion prefix terminated by ` -> `, target wrapped via `_record(...)` with operation/text metadata. Tests mirror the existing pattern: extend `test_ppl_circuit_coverage_v2_slices_include_basic_functionality_families` (or add a `code_semantics` analogue), add a `test_code_semantics_targets_match_metadata` that recomputes each target from `metadata`, and add the family to the leak/format assertion set.

## Description
Confirm FA4 execution path is using SM90-capable kernels on target hardware and quantify the impact relative to baseline.

Parent tracker: #6693

### Definition of Done

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue + parent tracker #6693 (accepts "SM90 row visible **or code-path proof**")
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (FA4 PRs/issues)
- [x] Trace FA4 arch dispatch on H100/SM90
- [x] Confirm production Grug d2560 shape (head_dim, GQA)
- [x] Post code-path proof + what's needed to fully close

This is verification work, not a code change — no PR. Fully closing the DoD needs the May215/`FA4PROFILE` artifact + an H100 profiling run (neither reachable from this environment), so this comment supplies the **code-path proof** half of the parent's acceptance bar.

# Research

On H100 (compute capability 9.0 → `arch=90`), the production Grug MoE attention shape routes the FA4/CuTe **backward** through the native upstream SM90 launcher added in #6613. The forward is the arch-agnostic Grug segmented CuTe kernel (no native-SM90 variant); only the backward has the SM80/SM120-compat vs native-SM90 split, and the backward is what May208 flagged as the top hotspot (#6613).

The native SM90 backward is gated on three conditions, all satisfied by the production d2560 shape:

1. `kernel_config.sm90_backward is not None` — set only for `arch_family == 9` (H100).
2. `qhead_per_kvhead > 1` — GQA. Production uses 4:1.
3. `q.shape[-1] == 128` — head_dim 128. Production `hidden_head_ratio=128` ⇒ `head_dim == 128`.

Otherwise the path falls back to `segmented_flash_attention_backward_launcher(..., compute_arch=90)` — compiled for SM90 but the slower segmented fork, i.e. the pre-#6613 behavior. So "FA4 SM90 active" hinges precisely on the shape being D128 GQA; MHA or non-128 head_dim silently takes the compat launcher even on SM90.

**Relevant code**
- [`_fa4_cute.py#L117-L128`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute.py#L117-L128) — `_gpu_compute_arch()`, H100 → `arch=90`
- [`_fa4_cute_config.py#L68-L80`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute_config.py#L68-L80) — `arch_family==9` sets `backward_arch=90` + `sm90_backward`
- [`_fa4_cute_backend.py#L158-L182`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute_backend.py#L158-L182) — native SM90 gate (`sm90_backward is not None and GQA and D128`)
- [`_fa4_cute_backend.py#L184-L196`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute_backend.py#L184-L196) — compat fallback `compute_arch=backward_arch`
- [`heuristic.py#L113-L114`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/heuristic.py#L113-L114) — `hidden_head_ratio=128` ⇒ head_dim 128, GQA 4:1

# Proposed approach (for the owner, @rav)

Code-path proof above is sufficient for the parent's "code-path proof" branch. To also satisfy the DoD's *per-step attribution report with FA4 timing/share*:

1. **Confirm in the existing profile.** Point the xprof analysis (`.agents/skills/profile-training/SKILL.md`) at the May215 / `…-FA4PROFILE-…` XPlane. The native SM90 backward shows as upstream `FlashAttentionBackwardSm90` kernels (preprocess + mainloop + postprocess, [`_fa4_cute_backend.py#L274-L290`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute_backend.py#L274-L290)); the compat path shows the segmented backward launcher instead. Presence of the former = SM90 active.
2. **Or a fresh readable proof.** A short H100 run on the d2560 shape with `enable_hlo_proto=true` (SKILL.md "profile options") yields named-scope attribution; assert the backward kernel name is the SM90 variant and report its per-step share.
3. **If inactive:** the only realistic miss is the shape not meeting the D128-GQA gate at [`_fa4_cute_backend.py#L158`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_fa4_cute_backend.py#L158) — verify `qhead_per_kvhead`/`head_dim` on the launched config rather than assuming the heuristic default.

- [`launch_cw_scale.py#L64-L69`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/launch_cw_scale.py#L64-L69) — known OOM boundary: peak mem ∝ batch×seq via replicated FSDP intermediate

# Proposed Approach (for @rav to run)

**128-GPU mesh.** `SCALE_GPU_REPLICAS=16` (16×8=128). With default `SCALE_EXPERT_AXIS=8`, `SCALE_REPLICA_AXIS=1`: `data_axis=128/8=16`, `batch_shards=1*16*8=128` → `SCALE_BATCH` must be a multiple of **128**.

**Max-BS sweep** (find OOM boundary; mem ∝ batch×seq, replicated FSDP intermediate per L64-67):
```
RUN_ID=bs-sweep SCALE_GPU_REPLICAS=16 SCALE_BATCH={128,256,384,512} \
  SCALE_STEPS=20 SCALE_CHECKPOINTS=local SCALE_TRACKER=wandb \
  SCALE_PROFILER_STEPS=5 uv run experiments/grug/moe/launch_cw_scale.py
```
Try `SCALE_REMAT=save_moe` (keeps tagged MoE dispatch tensors, avoids re-running EP collectives in backward) and `SCALE_MP=params=bfloat16,...` (halves FSDP gather bytes) to push BS higher.

**XLA flags** — set via the launcher shell, forwarded by `dispatch.py`. Candidates for fwd+bwd throughput: `--xla_gpu_enable_latency_hiding_scheduler=true`, `--xla_gpu_enable_pipelined_all_gather/reduce_scatter/all_reduce=true`, `--xla_gpu_all_reduce_combine_threshold_bytes` / `all_gather_combine_threshold_bytes` tuning. (PGLE is tracked separately in #6697.)

**Deliverables** (per DoD): max-safe BS at 128 GPUs; one full-config measured 128-GPU run with MFU; MFU vs N2/N4/N8 table; update the row in parent #6693.

If you'd rather I land a small enabling change instead (e.g. an `SCALE_XLA_FLAGS` convenience knob, or a scaling-sweep harness), say so and I'll open a scoped PR.

issues.author: mcwitt
issues.body:
The ragged all-to-all EP backend hangs at the d6144 hero scale (11 racks, 704 GPUs) within the first hundred steps, on both attempts of the 2026-09-02 deployment. The train step never completes on one rack, the other ten spin in the next AllReduce, and levanter's progress watchdog kills the gang 15 minutes later (`No progress after train_step_started for 909.8 seconds (timeout 900.0); terminating with exit code 124`). No rank logs an error: nothing from NCCL, XLA, CUDA (no Xid), the allocator, or Kubernetes. The hero was rolled back to `04751985c7` (pooled-wave backend), which resumed cleanly from the same checkpoint.

Deployment: main `8e48cdb3ca`, run `hero-ragged_a2a-ep-step54k` resuming `hero-12d8b6f0-dee637` from its `step-54000` permanent checkpoint (#8868), `HERO_WATCH_INTERVAL = 10`, `--xla_gpu_experimental_ragged_all_to_all_use_device_kernel=true --xla_enable_nccl_symmetric_buffers_for_collectives=raggedalltoall`, jax 0.11.1, NCCL 2.30.7. Coordinator `/marin/hero-ragged_a2a-ep-step54k-coord-aade2815`; both attempts ran on the same 176 nodes.

- Attempt 0: steps 54001–54070 completed normally (loss tracks the pooled-wave run step for step at −0.006 nats, drops 3.4e-2 → <1e-4, MFU 20.5 → 23.4%, peak HBM 103.6 GiB). Step 54071 started at 00:23:30Z and never finished; killed 00:38:46Z.
- Attempt 1: restored the same checkpoint, completed step 54000 at 00:45:38Z (loss 1.2364, identical to attempt 0), then hung on step 54001; killed ~01:01Z.

Both hangs are on the first plain train step after a `diagnostic_watch_step` step (54070 → 54071 after seven clean alternations; 54000 → 54001 on the first). The plain and watch steps are two XLA executables that share the NCCL symmetric-memory arena for the ragged all-to-all: each registers its own window at the arena base (`AcquireSymmetricMemory`, `CollectiveMemoryCache`), and equal footprints coexist. #8861 is the same design failing the other way: an executable with a *different* footprint (the capacity-limited eval) makes the next train step fail with `ncclGroupEnd() failed: invalid argument`. Here the footprints are equal and the failure is a silent hang instead of an error, so #8859 (dropless eval only) removes the crash but not this.

Evidence that the hang sits on one rack's EP domain rather than a node fault:

- NCCL RAS (periodic `STATUS` from process 0, `telemetry_v1.levanter`): six minutes into each hang, 64 cross-rack communicators show an AllReduce operation-count skew of exactly 3 (attempt 0: min 10509 / max 10512 at 00:29:43Z; attempt 1: 190 / 193 at 00:52:30Z) and the 704-rank communicator a skew of 2. Before the hangs every communicator was in sync. One member per cross-rack communicator behind by the same count is one whole rack that never entered the step's trailing AllReduces.
- Iris per-task CPU (`iris.task`): exactly 16 of 176 tasks ran at ~4.0 cores while the other 160 ran at ~8.0 during each hang, i.e. one rack in a different wait state from the ranks busy-polling in AllReduce. Attempt 0: tasks 128–143 (zone 129, nodes `s38vxs64 s45sxs64 s51vxs64 s5xvxs64 s69vxs64 s7htxs64 s7qvxs64 s8ktxs64 s8mtxs64 s8yvxs64 s9jvxs64 s9lrxs64 scspxs64 scssxs64 sd8sxs64 shmsxs64`). Attempt 1: tasks 64–79, a different rack on the same node set.
- py-spy thread dumps (`iris process profile threads`) of tasks 0, 83, and 140 during attempt 0: every rank's main thread inside `train_step` (`train.py:1176`), no Python-side wait; the hang is below XLA's dispatch.
- No node conditions or events on either rack; the cluster's six `HPCVerification=Fail` nodes are elsewhere.

The stall-triggered verbose RAS capture (`trigger = stall`) published nothing in either attempt, so the rank-level view that would name the stuck ranks and the pending collective is missing; the periodic sample is all we have. Neither a 200-step 1-rack smoke restoring the same checkpoint (20 watch/plain alternations) nor the 11,420-step d768 rung reproduced it, so the failure needs more than one rack, i.e. more than one EP domain sharing the job.

Side observations from the same deployment: a cold compile at this shape took 22.9 min for the watch executable plus 6.6 min for the plain one; the data loader's second 64-item prefetch took 920 s (overlapped by compile) where the pooled-wave hero's restarts took under 100 s.

Done when: the ragged backend runs at 11 racks through at least several hundred steps with watch steps enabled without a hang, or the hang is reproduced at smaller multi-rack scale with a GPU-side stack (CUDA core dump / `cuda-gdb` on a stuck rank) that names the kernel or collective.

Related: #8861 (symmetric-window overlap between executables), #8859, #8868, #8506 (hero status log). Side-by-side trial report: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/ep_change:-hero-ragged-a2a-swap,-200-step-trial--VmlldzoxNzg1ODIzMA==

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 The mechanism this issue describes is not what the hung run did, and the root cause is still open. Recording what has been ruled out so the next attempt does not repeat it.

The hero had one train executable, not two alternating ones. `launch_scaling_ladder.py:216` sets `WatchMode.INLINE` at the deployed commit `8e48cdb3ca`, so `_make_diagnostic_watch_step` is never built (`train.py:906`), `jit_train_step` computes watch stats on every step, and `step % 10 == 0` only decides whether the host logs them. Step 54071 was byte-identical to 54070 at the XLA and NCCL level. The working pooled-wave hero carries the identical watch config and does not hang.

The capacity-limited evaluator was already disabled. `c3f51e5250` (#8859) is an ancestor of `8e48cdb3ca`, and the dropless evaluator uses `sonic_cute`, which has no all-to-all and registers no symmetric window.

Window aliasing is present but was not the trigger. Two `jit_train_step` executables per rank each register a window at `0xbf80000000`; the cause is now known and is a step-counter sharding mismatch (details in #8861). What turns that aliasing into the `ncclGroupEnd` error is a third executable with a smaller footprint, and no such executable was running here.

Ruled out with evidence, all on one rack at the hero's shape, data and checkpoint unless noted. GIN: the device kernel logs `lsa_size=64 num_ranks=64 gin=false cta_count=152 num_updates_per_replica=6`, and forcing `lsa_size < num_ranks` produces `Device kernel skipped: lsa_size=32 num_ranks=64 requires GIN` followed by a hard `RaggedAllToAll fallback to NCCL is not allowed`, so `SupportsGin()` is false in this configuration. That also proves every hero EP domain was a single NVLink domain, since a domain spanning two would have failed loudly rather than stalled. CTA co-residency: the LSA barrier is per-slot, not grid-cooperative — `blockIdx.x` selects a barrier slot and CTA k rendezvouses only with CTA k on its peers — and at `__launch_bounds__(128, 8)` the 152-CTA grid uses a fraction of the device, so `0de14631ea` did not regress residency and the comment in that patch claiming the whole grid must be resident is wrong. `core_count` divergence: every rank reports `cta_count=152`. Hardware: the task-index-to-node map is identical across both attempts and the two stuck 16-task slices share no node. Allocator address churn: `Buffer allocations changed address between module jit_train_step executions` fires only for `parameter` and `live-out` entries, never `temp`, so the arena backing the window is stable. Ragged metadata: `CheckRaggedAllToAllBounds` passed 160 of 160 checks on the same HLO operands the device kernel consumes. NCCL 2.31.2: tested, identical failure (see #8861).

One rack does not reproduce it. Attempts covered two 32-GPU EP domains in one rack (161 steps, clean), raised collective overlap (dies of NaN at step 2, which is #8317's corruption and a different regime), NCCL channel contention, forcing the GIN branch, and a full-fidelity control at 48 layers with mixture data restored from the same `step-54000` checkpoint. The remaining differences at eleven racks — cross-rack collectives sharing the GPUs, and a 704-rank communicator — cannot be built inside one NVLink domain.

What survives is a stall in the LSA barrier that cannot report itself. XLA calls `ncclLsaBarrierSession::sync` in the no-timeout form, and NCCL sets `abortFlag` only `if (isInternal)` (`src/dev_runtime.cc:1175`), so a user-created devComm has none and no watchdog, abort or CUDA error can fire. The barrier epoch is an absolute counter that persists across launches and is zeroed once at `ncclDevCommCreate`, so any divergence is permanent.

Three instrumentation gaps made both attempts undiagnosable, and should be fixed before the next one. The stall diagnostic is never wired: `train.py:968` calls `progress_watchdog.create(process_index=...)` with no `diagnostic=`, so `diagnostic_timeout` stays unset and the stall capture publishes nothing. If it were wired it would run on the wrong process, because `ProgressWatchdogConfig.create` returns `None` for the entire watchdog when `diagnostic_timeout` is set and `process_index != 0`. And the watchdog's `startup_grace_period` defaulted to one hour, which covered attempt 1's entire hang — that run was killed by hand, not by the watchdog.

For the next eleven-rack attempt: set `TF_CPP_MIN_LOG_LEVEL=0` alongside `TF_CPP_VMODULE=ragged_all_to_all_thunk=3,nccl_symmetric_memory=3,gpu_executable=5`, and `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` with `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=REG,INIT,COLL`. `TF_CPP_VMODULE` alone emits nothing, and `NCCL_DEBUG=WARN` emits nothing for this failure class. A diagnostic PJRT build on `marin-community/xla` branch `mcwitt/8870-barrier-timeout` bounds both LSA barrier waits with NCCL's timeout overloads and records the stalled rank, barrier slot and phase, so the next occurrence names itself instead of producing fifteen minutes of silence. It also builds the device kernels against the NCCL the runtime loads: `tensorflow.bazelrc` pins `HERMETIC_NCCL_VERSION=2.29.7` while the runtime installs 2.30.7, and the timeout API exists only in the newer headers.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Follow-up on one hypothesis worth keeping open: that this is the same class of bug as #8861, namely a sharding JAX infers rather than one the code specifies, going wrong only once `replica_dcn` is a real axis.

Partial test on one rack. A single rack can make that axis non-degenerate by splitting into several expert domains, so: `--expert-axis-size 32` (giving `replica_dcn=2`) with `--num-experts 192` to keep six local experts per GPU and the hero's memory profile, 48 layers, inline watch, with the #8861 step-counter fix applied. Result was 64 arena windows, 64 `jit(train_step)` compilations across 64 ranks, and a per-leaf `Format` diff reporting `identical across the step`. No second state-sharding mismatch appears when the replica axis becomes real, and the #8861 fix holds there.

That does not close the hypothesis. It covers the train state only, at replica width 2, inside one NVLink domain and one process group. It does not cover batch sharding over `_BATCH_AXES = ("replica_dcn", "data", "expert")`, intermediates inside the step, or device ordering across 704 devices in 176 processes. Ordering is the part that matters here: `compact_grug_mesh` builds the mesh by reshaping `jax.devices()` in process order, while a `GSPMDSharding` carries the client's default device order, and the two coincide trivially when `replica_dcn=1`. A disagreement that resolves differently on different racks is the only proposed source of rank-dependent behaviour that survives, which is what a failure hitting one rack of eleven — a different one on each attempt — requires.

The direct test is a dump comparison, and it was not possible before now. `hero_grug_trainer_config` left `sharding_dump_path=None`, so `dump_grug_state_sharding_run_artifact` wrote to the pod-local `logs/` directory and the hung run's dump died with its pod. The ladder now writes it under the run's output path, so the next multi-rack run leaves a dump that can be diffed against a one-rack dump directly. That needs no special build and costs nothing.

Also worth recording for anyone reproducing this: `--expert-axis-size 32` at the hero's 384 experts puts twelve local experts on each GPU instead of six and OOMs at 158 GiB. Halve the expert count to hold the per-GPU profile fixed.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 An eleven-rack reproduction attempt on 2026-09-03 did not reproduce the hang, but it eliminated data- and state-dependence by direct measurement and turned up a version skew that reframes the failure. Root cause is still open.

**The reproduction was faithful, and it did not hang.** Two jobs at 11 racks, 235 steps in total (164 then 71), restored from the same `step-54000` both failed attempts used, at the hero's exact shape. It matched attempt 0's loss to ±0.00007 nats over the whole overlapping range and sat -0.0058 nats against the pooled-wave control, reproducing the -0.006 offset reported above; MFU 22-23% against attempt 0's 23.4%. It carried the same transport (`lsa_size=64 num_ranks=64 gin=false cta_count=152`) and the same symmetric-window aliasing this issue describes: 1408 arena-window registrations across 704 ranks, exactly two per rank, alongside 1408 `jit_train_step` compilations.

**The hang is not a function of the data or the model state.** Attempt 0 completed step 54071 (`train_loss` 1.23687 at 00:23:35.14Z) and hung on the next one. The replay ran through that step and kept going. Since the loss agrees to seven significant figures, the batch, the routing, the optimizer state and the arithmetic there are identical to the run that died. Combined with attempt 1 hanging at 54001 from the same restored state, the trigger is timing, not state, and the failure cannot be forced by choosing a checkpoint or a step.

**On the statistics, stated carefully.** Hero exposure was 75 step-attempts with two hangs; the reproduction ran 235 clean. A one-sided test gives p ≈ 0.06 — suggestive that something differs between the two setups, but not significant. Job-steps are the right unit here, not rack-steps: the hang is a job-level event, so counting all 11 racks as independent trials overstates the evidence.

**Candidates eliminated since the last update.** Concurrent checkpoint I/O: `grep "Saving checkpoint"` across every task log in both attempts returns zero hits, so neither attempt ever wrote a checkpoint. Online W&B: per-step tracker cost was 3.73-3.84 ms at every detail step and the wandb thread was idle in `selectors.select` at the py-spy dump. The NCCL RAS probe: it ran in both attempts at a 600 s cadence taking 69-83 ms, and the 00:29:43.8Z poll *succeeded during the hang*, so process 0 and NCCL's in-process listener were responsive while the gang was wedged. A rank silently falling off the device-kernel path: `RaggedAllToAllThunk::RunCollective` returns `InvalidArgument("RaggedAllToAll fallback to NCCL is not allowed")` when `xla_gpu_allow_ragged_all_to_all_nccl_send_recv_fallback` is false, which is the deployed setting, so such a rank fails loudly rather than desynchronising quietly, and no attempt logged an error. Two ragged kernels sharing barrier slots: the hero forces `--xla_gpu_experimental_parallel_collective_overlap_limit=1`, so collectives cannot be co-resident.

**The version skew, which is a real defect on its own.** `tensorflow.bazelrc:192` pins `HERMETIC_NCCL_VERSION="2.29.7"` while the runtime resolves to 2.30.7. NCCL's `ncclDevCommCompat_v22907` shim then forces `ginType = NONE` and gates `deviceApiSupport` on `ncclTeamLsa(comm).nRanks == comm->nRanks`. That explains structurally why `SupportsGin()` is false — it was never a configuration choice — and why the device kernel only ever runs on the per-rack EP64 clique, so eleven racks are eleven independent barrier domains whose hazard adds with rack count while nothing couples them. It also means the deployed kernel is compiled without 2.30's bounded `sync(..., timeoutCycles)` overload and without its system-scope release fence in `arrive`, which is exactly why the stall cannot report itself.

**Leading remaining hypothesis.** A stray peer store from the copy loop landing inside the devComm resource window and corrupting the barrier state. Every symmetric window, including the one holding the barrier epochs, lives in the same `devr` VA reservation with a common `stride4G`, and the barrier epoch is an absolute per-slot counter that is never reset or exchanged, so any divergence is permanent: a peer that falls behind makes its partner spin on a comparison that wraps to ~2^32, with `abortFlag == nullptr` for user devComms and no timeout. One sub-case has a matching upstream fix we do not carry: NCCL `0d7243b`, "Mitigate loadConst `__ldg` regression", replaces the non-coherent `__ldg` read of `lsaFlatBase`/`stride4G` with a plain dereference, and those window pointers are rewritten at run time by `ncclDevrReplaceSegmentWindowsIfNeeded`.

**Instrumentation now exists, and did not before.** `CUDA_` was missing from the dispatcher's forwarded env prefixes, so the GPU core-dump variables could never reach a training gang; with that fixed the driver creates one dump pipe per rank. A dump must be taken with `CUDA_COREDUMP_GENERATION_FLAGS=skip_abort,skip_global_memory,skip_constbank_memory`: the default writes 62 GB and SIGABRTs the process, which killed all 64 ranks of a smoke gang and lost the dump with the pod, while the flags give 283 MB. Even so it is terminal within about two minutes (measured at 2:36 and 1:55), so it must trigger, read and upload in one round trip and go last. A dump taken mid-kernel names the resident kernel and gives a per-block state table, which matters because the LSA barrier is per-slot indexed by `blockIdx.x` and that table therefore names the diverged slots directly. NCCL RAS `VERBOSE STATUS` can also be triggered by hand during a hang, answering in ~4 ms with the per-collective min/max that showed the AllReduce skew of exactly 3. Do not attach `cuda-gdb` to a live process: an attach to PID 1 returned nothing in 150 s and took the gang down.

**Next.** A wheel built with the device kernels compiled against the run-time NCCL 2.30.7 exists as `marin-xla-pjrt-candidate-ca0716a2da95`; it removes the skew, adds bounded LSA barriers that record rank, slot and phase, extends the bounds check to the device path, and promotes the transport line to INFO. It is being validated on one rack. The one structural difference between the hero and the reproduction that survives all of the above is that the hero runs `broadcast_one_to_all` inside `checkpointer.on_step` on every step — a cross-host collective on a `(176, 4)` mesh whose rank groups exist nowhere else in the job — while the reproduction, with `save_checkpoints=False`, never creates a checkpointer at all (`train.py:1031`). A next window should restore that at zero I/O cost with `--save-checkpoints --checkpoint-minutes 600`, and a one-rack `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,REG` A/B on that flag would first confirm the communicator inventory actually differs.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 One actionable gap found while testing a prediction of the barrier-stall hypothesis, worth recording separately because it is cheap to fix and independent of everything else above.

The hypothesis predicts the stuck rack's GPUs were saturated during the hang, spinning inside a resident device kernel, as opposed to idle because the kernel never launched. That is directly checkable from `iris.task`, which carries `accelerator_util_pct` and `accelerator_mem_bytes`. During attempt 0's hang window (00:23:36-00:38:43Z) **both fields are null in all 2,636 samples**.

The query is sound: the same rows reproduce the known CPU signature exactly, with the stuck rack at 4.04 cores against 7.85 on the healthy racks, matching the 4.0-vs-8.0 split reported in this issue. So the nulls are a collection gap rather than a query error.

That gap is expensive out of proportion to its size. GPU utilisation separates "spinning in a resident kernel" from "kernel never launched" on its own, which is the first branch any analysis of this failure has to take, and it needs no core dump, no rebuilt wheel and no reproduction. Enabling accelerator telemetry on the hero gang is the cheapest single change that would improve the next occurrence.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Follow-up with the experimental record from the overnight session. Four more mechanisms eliminated, three of them by direct experiment rather than inference, and two of them hypotheses raised in this issue's earlier comments. Root cause still not determined; what follows is what a next attempt should not spend time on.

**Residency starvation is refuted.** The concern that the ragged kernel's grid cannot stay fully resident is real in principle — the LSA barrier makes CTA k wait on CTA k of every peer, and a CTA that is never scheduled stalls its peers forever, while the already-resident CTAs spin holding their SMs and never yield, so nothing can free what the missing CTAs need. The pre-patch wheel `marin-xla-pjrt-20260828-c9526e8c0272` is maximally exposed to this: it sizes the grid as `kGridSmMultiplier * core_count` where `kGridSmMultiplier = kRaggedAllToAllDeviceKernelCtasPerSm = 8`, i.e. 1216 CTAs against exactly 1216 CTA slots at `__launch_bounds__(128, 8)`. Zero headroom, and its own comment states the requirement. Run at hero shape on one rack it completed **176 steps, roughly 8,400 ragged launches each needing all 1216 CTAs resident simultaneously, with no stall**. Foreign occupancy during the ragged kernel is therefore effectively zero and starvation at the shipped wheel's 8x margin is implausible.

Incidentally, that wheel is about 11% faster: 16.4 s/it and 23.8% MFU against the shipped 18.3 s/it and 21.5%. The grid patch buys a margin this result suggests is not needed, which is worth revisiting on its own merits.

**The autotune-cache race is not this.** The shared node-local `/cache/xla/per-fusion-autotune` race (#8896) is real and caused a hero retry, but it cannot reach the train step: a 40-step run at a never-compiled shape wrote **zero** autotune results, because this model's heavy GEMMs are Marin's own CUTLASS kernels rather than XLA-autotuned fusions. Autotuning fires only for incidental ops such as the checkpoint slice, so divergent results there cannot change the train step's fusion selection, buffer assignment, arena size or window registration.

**Cross-rack GDR cannot corrupt the barrier.** `devr->lsaFlatBase` is a dedicated `cuMemAddressReserve`; NCCL's network buffers are separate `ncclCudaCalloc` allocations registered through `ncclNetRegMr`. A NIC can only write inside a registered memory region, and a write outside it is rejected by hardware with a completion error rather than landing silently elsewhere.

**Divergent devComm Requirements would be the cleanest mechanism, and both routes to it are closed.** Two ranks requesting different `Requirements` get different devComms, hence different barrier buffers, and since devComm creation is collective each would wait in a barrier the other never joins — silent and permanent, needing no epoch divergence at all. But divergent `lsa_size` takes the `has_remote_peers && !SupportsGin()` branch and fails loudly with `InvalidArgument("RaggedAllToAll fallback to NCCL is not allowed")`, and no hero rank logged an error; while divergent `core_count` would be a static per-node property, and the failure moved between two node sets the forensics established are disjoint.

**The kernel's copy loops are bounded.** Both the LSA loop and the inner copy terminate on `num_lsa_updates` and `hi` respectively, `hi` is clamped to each update's own extent, and the GIN branch is dead in this build. Combined with the eliminations above, the barrier is the only place this can hang — that part is now established by construction rather than inference.

**Reproduction attempts, all null:** eleven racks at hero shape (235 steps); maximum executable churn with four executables cycling (~300 steps); registration determinism (all 64 ranks byte-identical, 29 registrations, same order and offsets); cold autotune at a novel shape; zero-headroom residency (176 steps); four EP cliques on one rack (189 steps); and a second transfer geometry at `--latent-dim 2048 --capacity-factor 1.37`, which changes stride and alignment in every offset the copy computes (192 steps).

A single rack cannot reach the remaining space, and the reason is structural: symmetric windows are registered only by the ragged path (`--xla_enable_nccl_symmetric_buffers_for_collectives=raggedalltoall`), so extra communicators and expert-domain splitting do not emulate eleven racks. Closing this needs the failure state observed. The capture path is now armed by default on the ragged transport, so the next occurrence should name itself rather than produce fifteen minutes of silence.
