🤖

## Open-MOPD end-to-end reproduction: reproducibility report

[Public source document](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/open-mopd-reproduce.md)

This guide reproduces **stage three** of the [authors' Open-MOPD recipe](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/open-mopd-experiment-overview.md): distill the three released RL teachers into one student, starting from the released MixSFT checkpoint. It records the exact chain that produced our evaluated **step-32** policy. It does not claim that we trained the base-to-MixSFT model or the three RL teachers ourselves. For those earlier stages, use the [authors' paper and code](https://github.com/BytedTsinghua-SIA/Open-MOPD) and [released data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/BytedTsinghua-SIA/Open-MOPD-Data).

The ready-to-use checkpoint is [open-athena/MarinSkyRL-Open-MOPD-SmolLM3-3B-step-32](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/MarinSkyRL-Open-MOPD-SmolLM3-3B-step-32). The [training trace archive](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-open-mopd-native-traces) stores retained rollouts and inline evaluation outputs. The [score files](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/tree/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/native-step-32) and [comparison note](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/notes/2026-09-18-open-mopd-publication-comparison.md) are separate from training traces.

## 1. Prepare access and verify inputs

You need the pinned MarinSkyRL source revisions below, the root `uv.lock`, an eight-H100-class GPU allocation, object-store output space, and read access to the released public models and dataset. Our original jobs ran on Iris cluster `cw-rno2a` at **interactive** priority. New users must substitute their own cluster, object-store paths, and credentials; the copied scripts contain the original operator's absolute paths. Before any new launch, check idle or batch-occupied capacity and the interactive budget as required by the local operations policy.

The input files here are not descriptions: they are byte copies of the launch inputs. Verify them before launch:

```bash
shasum -a 256 launch-records/inputs/weighted_200step_schedule.parquet
shasum -a 256 launch-records/inputs/aime24_inline.parquet
```

Expected SHA-256 values are `01d9c3904b13324f218f61e51db187e52872c641a466025b300295eef707dae5` and `120aa8b103ef0c76fab1e67bdca94b0ec365744b0dac190c3d9c0c3b4e563bde`, respectively. The schedule has 204,800 rows in 200 row groups: 1,024 prompts per step. Its [build manifest](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/inputs/weighted_200step_schedule.manifest.json) and [builder](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/scripts/build_open_mopd_weighted_schedule.py) explain the source records and ordering. The original launches read the same bytes from `s3://marin-us-east-02a/iris/cw-rno2a/experiments/open-mopd-repro/20260916d/native-inputs/`.

Pin the inputs that otherwise might drift:

| Component | Repository | Commit or revision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Student initialization | `BytedTsinghua-SIA/Open-MOPD-SmolLM3-3B-MixSFT` | `c9e7bad031667828656ead188d7e8ea162c048a4` |
| Math teacher | `BytedTsinghua-SIA/Open-MOPD-SmolLM3-3B-RL-Math` | `5e901bb626b69d711074d2832c41ce1aa4232da8` |
| Code teacher | `BytedTsinghua-SIA/Open-MOPD-SmolLM3-3B-RL-Code` | `e2ce9beec52381350edcdaefebfd08ea67c21b42` |
| IF teacher | `BytedTsinghua-SIA/Open-MOPD-SmolLM3-3B-RL-IF` | `8948051a805883e2db988cae4522de3c29d1d112` |
| Original native code | `marin-community/MarinSkyRL` | `4ce9717817772edd8645db79d1978cd72c59bb33` |
| Fast-gate code | `marin-community/MarinSkyRL` | `8fd72853ca73372baa27cca4191c4d200902ac05` |
| Fast-full code | `marin-community/MarinSkyRL` | `12e6da9eacddf02d844b7f9e90ba5370ff45761b` |

The [original](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/source-original/cloud/iris/configs/open_mopd_fidelity.json), [fast-gate](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/source-fast-gate/cloud/iris/configs/open_mopd_fidelity.json), and [fast-full](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/source/cloud/iris/configs/open_mopd_fidelity.json) configs each have a matching source snapshot of the learner entrypoint, `pyproject.toml`, and `uv.lock` in their respective directories. These were extracted from the three source commits, not copied from the current worktree. The selected [vLLM wheel](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-gpu-wheelhouse/resolve/main/linux-x86_64/cp312/20260916-opd-vllm/vllm-0.20.1rc1.dev1486%2Bmarinopdcu12916176bf86.precompiled-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl) has SHA-256 `29f478ad84bf949817bf9a65bb6d7ece3491d9ce4ec02eacd8641f13ddaca07d`. The original image was `ghcr.io/marin-community/marinskyrl-opd-repro@sha256:7c4f1275c8a6c53b94218524c6f7601808662cb7f429e2ece6d05854ad804540`. Keep these pins when comparing results.

## 2. Follow the actual step-32 checkpoint lineage

The evaluated model is **not** one uninterrupted 32-step job. It is a deliberate continuation through two seeded checkpoint copies. Keep the three output roots separate:

| Segment | Source | Output | Steps on selected lineage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Original | [launch script](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/scripts/launch_open_mopd_native_full.py), [record](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/original/manifest.json) | `open-mopd-native-20260916c` | 1–4 |
| Fast gate | [seed](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/scripts/seed_open_mopd_native_fast_gate.py), [launch](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/scripts/launch_open_mopd_native_fast_gate.py), [records](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/tree/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/fast-gate) | `open-mopd-native-fast-gate-20260917a` | 5–6 |
| Fast full | [seed](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/scripts/seed_open_mopd_native_fast_full.py), [launch](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/scripts/launch_open_mopd_native_fast_full.py), [records](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/tree/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/fast-full) | `open-mopd-native-fast-full-20260917a` | 7–32 |

To replay the *same launch sequence*, check out each listed source commit in turn, set up the input and output locations, and run the corresponding scripts from the repository root with `--submit`. Run each seed only after its preceding job has produced and verified the required step checkpoint, and run each continuation only after its seed succeeds. Without `--submit`, the scripts print their planned actions. The selected checkpoint's command sequence was:

```bash
python launch-records/scripts/launch_open_mopd_native_full.py --gate --submit
python launch-records/scripts/launch_open_mopd_native_full.py --submit
python launch-records/scripts/seed_open_mopd_native_fast_gate.py --submit
python launch-records/scripts/launch_open_mopd_native_fast_gate.py --submit
python launch-records/scripts/seed_open_mopd_native_fast_full.py --submit
python launch-records/scripts/launch_open_mopd_native_fast_full.py --submit
```

The CPU-only `--gate` job succeeded before the original full run. Two other successful checks were performed in the campaign: a [colocated step-3 gate](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/scripts/launch_open_mopd_colocated_gate.py) on a separate branch and a [step-6 fast-export check](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/scripts/launch_open_mopd_native_fast_export.py). Neither changes the selected model's optimizer-state lineage. The independent full-suite evaluator is also a separate job, not a training continuation.

These scripts are **historical launch records**, not a portable one-command installer. They import campaign-local helpers, expect the old operator's worktree and Iris account, and may reflect later edits. For byte-exact trainer arguments, use each immutable S3-derived [`manifest.json`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/fast-full/manifest.json), especially its `command` array; for seed provenance, use each [`fork-manifest.json`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/fast-full/fork-manifest.json). The root manifests record the actual dataset URI and SHA-256, validation URI and SHA-256, source commit, checkpoint/export roots, and configured intervals. Adapt resource plumbing and paths to your environment while preserving the training values.

The final segment uses FSDP2 on four policy GPUs, four student vLLM rollout engines, and three pinned single-GPU vLLM teacher engines on one eight-H100 node. It hard-routes math, code, and IF prompts to the matching teacher. It uses the `student_topk_policy_surrogate` loss with `student_selected_topk` evidence (`k=16`), 1,024 rollout prompts, 256-prompt inner minibatches, learning rate `1.5e-6`, policy clip `0.2/0.28`, and no KL penalty. The schedule's prompt mix is 2:2:1; the initial target *gradient-token* shares are one-third each, with gap-following exponent 1. Checkpoints and inline AIME validation were configured every two steps. Read the manifest rather than transcribing this summary into a new config.

The original output continued separately past step 4, and the fast-full output continued to step 34 before the owner stopped it. Those extra checkpoints are **not** ancestors of the selected step-32 model. The [trace archive](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-open-mopd-native-traces) labels each segment, including side-branch and later steps.

## 3. Verify the checkpoint and evaluate

The step-32 FSDP2 policy was exported as six Hugging Face files at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/benjaminfeuer/skyrl/open-mopd-native-fast-full-20260917a/exports/global_step_32/policy/`. No format conversion beyond that export is required. The published [`model.safetensors`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/MarinSkyRL-Open-MOPD-SmolLM3-3B-step-32/blob/main/model.safetensors) must hash to `bb7326640142069bc2e1fba5f54f15e0cccb1ff861f34f318b372eaab7abaf4b`. The [evaluation manifest](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/native-step-32/evaluation-manifest.json) lists all six export hashes and the independent evaluator settings.

Run the [independent suite launcher](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/launch-records/scripts/launch_open_mopd_eval_with_punkt.py) against the exported policy, or use the matching evaluation configuration with your own scheduler. Score AIME24 and AIME25 over 30 questions × 64 sampled answers each, and IFEval over 541 prompts. The recorded results are [423/1,920](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/native-step-32/scores/aime24.json), [448/1,920](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/native-step-32/scores/aime25.json), and [403/541](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/native-step-32/scores/ifeval.json). “Mean@64” is the proportion of correct samples across all 1,920 AIME outputs, not 30 binary pass/fail values. LiveCodeBench v5/v6 and IFBench rollouts were generated, but we do not assert paper-comparable scores for those three datasets; do not invent a six-dataset total from the available score files.

## 4. Inspect or extend the evidence

The [trace dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-open-mopd-native-traces) contains retained student training trajectories from all three job roots and inline evaluation output records. Each trajectory carries its step, prompt, generated response, domain, and teacher-route metadata. These retained trajectory records **do not contain the per-token teacher log-probability tensors** used in the loss. Thus the archive establishes what the student generated and which teacher was routed, but does not reconstruct every teacher scoring call. The immutable teacher model revisions and exact loss/config/source pins above are the way to regenerate that evidence. See the trace dataset card for file coverage and archive format.

The [original authors' result](https://huggingface.co/BytedTsinghua-SIA/Open-MOPD-SmolLM3-3B-Final) is a separate model, not our step-32 export. The [three-benchmark comparison](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/notes/2026-09-18-open-mopd-publication-comparison.md) compares like-named evaluations but should not be read as proof that every benchmark version, grader, or full six-dataset score was matched. Retain both the raw score JSON and the run manifests when reporting any new result.

## Open-MOPD end-to-end reproduction: results

[Public source document](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/notes/2026-09-18-open-mopd-publication-comparison.md)

As of 2026-09-18, native MarinSkyRL at step 32 is within 0.47 percentage points of the published Open-MOPD result on AIME24, AIME25, and IFEval. The corrected authors-code control at step 84 is above the published math scores and 1.48 points below its IFEval score. This is a three-benchmark comparison, not a reproduction of the six-benchmark total.

| Benchmark | Published Open-MOPD, step 200 | Native MarinSkyRL, step 32 | Corrected authors-code control, step 84 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| AIME24, mean@64 | [21.98%][paper-table] | [22.03%][native-aime24] (423/1,920) | [22.71%][reference-aime24] (436/1,920) |
| AIME25, mean@64 | [22.86%][paper-table] | [23.33%][native-aime25] (448/1,920) | [24.27%][reference-aime25] (466/1,920) |
| IFEval, mean@1 | [74.49%][paper-table] | [74.49%][native-ifeval] (403/541) | [73.01%][reference-ifeval] (395/541) |

The published percentages are from Table 2 of the [paper][paper-table]. The authors' [released final model card][published-model] explicitly says that this model is training step 200 and repeats the same per-dataset scores. The paper's Appendix A.2/Table 8 separately lists **600 total steps** for the stage-three training setting. It does not establish that Table 2 was scored at step 600; the released model card identifies step 200 for the score-matched checkpoint. The 300-step trajectories discussed in the paper likewise do not change that checkpoint identification.

Our columns use the complete released-suite evaluation score files linked in the table. Each AIME percentage divides correct sampled answers by 1,920 outputs: 30 questions with 64 samples each. The IFEval denominator is 541 prompts. Scores are rounded to two decimal places here. The [native step-32 manifest][native-manifest] and [reference step-84 manifest][reference-manifest] identify the evaluation runs. The corrected reference [stopped after 84 optimizer steps][reference-stop-audit] when its single dataset epoch ran out, despite a configured 200-step ceiling. The [evidence bundle](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/README.md) records source locations and checksums. ## Open-MOPD end-to-end reproduction: timing and MFU

[Public source document](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/open-mopd-repro/timing/2026-09-18-open-mopd-step-time-flops.md)

TL;DR: On RNO2A H100×8, the corrected authors-code control averaged 937 seconds per completed optimizer step over its 84-step job. Native MarinSkyRL's four-engine continuation averaged 3,031 seconds over steps 22–33, including its every-two-step inline evaluation and checkpoint work (3.23× the reference wall time). Its non-cadence steps had a 2,225-second median. The original single-engine native run took 5,297 and 5,757 seconds at early steps 1 and 3; it was stopped by request after a complete step-22 checkpoint. Estimated student-training MFU is 0.78% for the fast native window and 2.52% for the reference **if** it processed the same number of tokens. These are not controlled throughput benchmarks: response lengths, checkpoint implementation, validation, and step windows differ.

| Implementation and window | Time per optimizer step | Comparison with corrected reference | What the time includes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Corrected authors-code reference, whole job through step 84 | 937 s mean (15.6 min) | 1.00× | Iris task wall duration 21 h 52 m 12.99 s divided by 84 actual steps; includes startup, inline validation, checkpointing, and exit. |
| Corrected authors-code reference, steps 1–2 | 933 s, 916 s (924 s mean) | 0.99× full-job mean | Logged step times; small early sample. |
| Native fast, steps 22–33 | 3,031 s mean (50.5 min) | 3.23× | Six cadence and six non-cadence steps; step timer encloses step-end callbacks. |
| Native fast, odd/non-cadence steps 23–33 | 2,225 s median (37.1 min) | 2.37× | Training, generation, and teacher scoring without the scheduled two-step validation/checkpoint callbacks. |
| Native fast, even/cadence steps 22–32 | 3,984 s median (66.4 min) | 4.25× | Includes scheduled validation/checkpoint callbacks; the timing gap does not isolate their individual costs. |
| Native original, early steps 1 and 3 | 5,297 s, 5,757 s (5,527 s mean) | 5.90× | Single rollout engine; two early observations, not its whole-run median. |

The fast run's odd-step means were about 997 s for generation, 762 s for teacher/student forward scoring, and 434 s for the policy update. The original run's step 3 spent 3,733 s in generation, 1,561 s in teacher/scoring, and 447 s in the policy update. Four rollout engines substantially reduced the observed generation cost; teacher/scoring remains a large part of native step time. Even-step total time is substantially larger than the sum of these three phases because the inclusive step timer encloses callback work. The corrected reference's domain teacher-scoring subcalls at step 1 were 73 s for math and about 61 s each for code and instruction following, but those subcalls alone are not directly comparable to the native forward-phase timer.

## MFU estimates

Model FLOPs utilization (MFU) divides the FLOPs required for the student model's forward and backward passes by available peak FLOPs over elapsed time. This follows the [PaLM definition](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume24/22-1144/22-1144.pdf): recomputation and other implementation-dependent work do not increase the numerator. This is an end-to-end training-job MFU, so the denominator includes rollout, teacher scoring, inline evaluation, checkpointing, and idle time even though those activities do not count as student training work.

The student and all three specialist teachers each declare 3,337,766,912 parameters. The fast native run logged a mean 9,312,140 scored response tokens across its 1,024 responses per step at steps 22–33. With P parameters and T scored response tokens, the first-order student-training model work is 6PT, or **186 PFLOPs per fast step**. The fast job's eight GPUs identify as H100 80GB HBM3. We assume H100 SXM dense BF16 peak of **989 TFLOP/s per GPU**, or **7.912 PFLOP/s for eight GPUs**. NVIDIA's [non-sparse peak table](https://github.com/NVIDIA/exemplar-performance) gives 989 TFLOP/s for H100 BF16; the [H100 specification](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/h100/) labels its higher BF16 figure as *with sparsity*, which is not appropriate here. The reference's resolved manifest still says A100×8, but Iris verified its actual job ran on H100×8.

| Run and timing window | Response tokens used in estimate | Elapsed time per step | Student-training MFU | OPD model-work ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Corrected reference, 84-step task wall time | **9.31M assumed**, not measured | 937 s | **2.52% conditional** | 4.19–5.03% conditional |
| Native fast, steps 22–33 pooled | 9.31M measured mean | 3,031 s mean | **0.78%** | 1.30–1.56% |
| Native fast, six odd steps pooled | 9.28M measured mean | 2,207 s mean | **1.06%** | 1.77–2.13% |
| Native fast, six even steps pooled | 9.34M measured mean | 3,854 s mean | **0.61%** | 1.02–1.23% |
| Native original, step 1 | 9.77M measured | 5,297 s | **0.47%** | 0.78–0.93% |

The OPD model-work ratio is **not conventional MFU**. It adds one student rollout forward (2PT), one routed-teacher forward (2PT), and optionally one separate student scoring forward (2PT) to the student update's 6PT. Thus its numerator is 10–12PT. The three specialists route different samples; this estimate does not charge three teacher forwards to every token. It is useful for accounting for this multi-model job, but it should not be compared with published single-model training MFUs.

For each row, student-training MFU = 6P × response tokens ÷ (8 × 989 TFLOP/s × elapsed seconds). Pooled fast rows use total tokens divided by total elapsed seconds, not the average of per-step percentages. The reference percentage is only a **same-token-workload scenario**: its corrected 84-step run lacks a recovered per-step token count for this window. Its actual MFU scales in proportion to its actual trained-token count divided by 9.31M. The original native row uses its observed step-1 count rather than the fast-run proxy. Including up to the configured 2,048 prompt tokens for each of 1,024 responses would raise a 9.31M-response-token numerator by at most about 22.5%; actual prompt lengths were not recovered.

These are analytical, response-token-only estimates. The 6PT approximation excludes sequence-length-dependent attention FLOPs, and the OPD range omits sampling/logit work, recomputation, communication, and optimizer arithmetic. Exact MFU needs the actual student training-token count and model-architecture FLOP accounting for each window; hardware FLOP utilization instead requires accelerator counters. The denominator includes long non-student phases, so these percentages cannot diagnose Tensor Core occupancy.

## Evidence and scope

- Native fast: live pod stdout WANDB_MIRROR training metrics for completed steps 22–33, captured in the [companion CSV](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/marinskyrl-opd-mopd-repro-artifacts/blob/main/artifacts/timing/2026-09-18-native-fast-steps-22-33.csv). Source job /benfeuer/open-mopd-native-fast-full-20260917a, RNO2A. Four historical preemptions occurred before this sampled window; the sampled log is one current attempt. The trainer source's inclusive step timer wraps callback work.
- Corrected reference: Iris controller terminal duration 21 h 52 m 12.99 s and control manifest; the job actually completed 84 optimizer steps because its single dataset epoch ended, although configured for 200. Campaign STATE.md records 932.963 s and 915.64 s for steps 1–2. Source job /benjaminfeuer/open-mopd-reference-corrected-20260917a, RNO2A.
- Native original: campaign STATE.md records full step 1 (5,296.519 s; 9,767,287 response tokens) and step 3 (5,757.3854 s), with phase timings. Source job /benjaminfeuer/open-mopd-native-full-20260916c, RNO2A. Its exact Iris job is killed by user request; 20 complete files totaling 18,469,880,397 bytes remain at s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/benjaminfeuer/skyrl/open-mopd-native-20260916c/checkpoints/global_step_22.
- The fast run was stopped by the owner after the sampled window. This report compares completed steps only; it does not project a 200-step finish time.

issues.title: MarinSkyRL OPD/MOPD: implementation and reproduction results

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Establish a reproducible baseline for an existing Snowball terminal agent on established computational biology benchmarks, with frozen weights. Start with a small diagnostic pilot, then expand to a fixed evaluation set for comparing subsequent checkpoints. Separate scientific errors from agent, serving, environment, and grading failures. Together AI is available for LLM judging, so judge access no longer limits benchmark selection. Prioritize BixBench's existing Harbor CLI adapter as the primary-suite candidate, continue the Terminal-Bench-Science smoke test, and validate ScienceAgentBench's bioinformatics tasks next.

## Description

Computational biology tasks combine coding, statistical analysis, scientific judgment, and domain tools. Snowball already has a post-trained terminal-agent checkpoint and measured performance with its matching harness in [#8225](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8225). We need to establish how that capability transfers to biological analysis.

The proposed starting model is [Snowball 67B-A2B Nemotron-Terminal, step 1888](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-sft-s3-nemotron-terminal-step1888/tree/680bec3ade494b61ead6861fa24fc4071f8dc294), evaluated through Harbor with its matching Terminus-2 terminal-agent harness. Confirm whether a newer checkpoint is preferred before fixing the baseline. Record each checkpoint separately.

Use Marin's existing evaluation launcher and Harbor integration where available. This issue tracks benchmark selection, integration readiness, runs, and findings. Substantial adapter changes can be linked as separate implementation work. New benchmarks, training, and tool-free biology evaluations are outside the first milestone.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Measure how often Snowball completes computational biology tasks under a fixed execution budget, and identify the dominant causes of failure. The initial baseline measures existing capability; it does not establish the causal benefit of coding training or imply an absence of biology exposure in the checkpoint's training data.

Scorer code and release inventories were checked on September 14–15, 2026. These readiness assessments are source inspections except for the GeneBench-Pro scorer checks and Terminal-Bench-Science oracle run described below. No Snowball biology baseline has completed.

September 17 planning update: Together AI is the available route for LLM judging; provider integration has not yet been tested in this effort. Its [OpenAI-compatible API](https://docs.together.ai/docs/inference/openai-compatibility) supports chat and structured outputs with a Together endpoint, API key, and model ID. A judge requirement is no longer a reason to defer a benchmark. Configure and test each evaluator's provider integration, including vision where needed. Pin the judge model, prompt, and settings; check reference, deliberately wrong, and ambiguous answers before a pilot. A replacement judge defines a separately reported evaluation variant until score comparability has been established.

Priority reflects integration readiness and scientific coverage. `Next check` identifies immediate readiness work; `Follow-up` covers additional integration or complementary coverage; `Resolve assets/protocol` requires obtaining restricted scoring assets or defining a grading procedure. Input access and resource requirements still need validation for each selected task.

| Priority | Benchmark and capability | Released scorer and reference material | Access and judge requirements | Harbor readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Next check: primary candidate | [BixBench v1.5, Harbor CLI](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/tree/main/adapters/bixbench): notebook-derived biological analysis questions | [Harbor judge code](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/0d67ca4b59206aca2734bf9fe0260ca79e08acb4/adapters/bixbench/src/bixbench/task-template/tests/llm_judge.py) and public reference answers are available. The adapter grades open answers with an LLM, including numeric/range answers. Upstream also releases a [deterministic multiple-choice grader](https://github.com/Future-House/BixBench/blob/49311180bdacb324c596f2e07596c126f2004008/bixbench/graders.py). | The pinned grader uses the OpenAI SDK, an API-key variable, a configurable model name, and structured-response parsing. Connect it to Together AI and validate parsing and grading. Upstream multiple-choice scoring uses a different question/answer protocol. | Adapter exists upstream and in Marin's fork. First primary-suite candidate: validate the Together judge and one task, then select a prespecified pilot across data capsules. Report the judge variant explicitly; the CLI protocol differs from the original notebook leaderboard. |
| Next check: smoke test | [Terminal-Bench-Science, life sciences](https://github.com/harbor-framework/terminal-bench-science): scientific workflows | Task-specific executable tests and reference fixtures are released. For the inspected [genomic-model-ranking task](https://github.com/harbor-framework/terminal-bench-science/tree/ff55a1b0810a5cc2ebac3ebb007cbe6a26aa2e3b/tasks/life-sciences/biology/genomic-model-ranking/tests), pytest checks predictions, rankings, and executable submissions against supplied fixtures and thresholds. | That task's verifier runs without network access or a judge API. Check other tasks individually. | Harbor-native. This task's oracle passed through Marin's Harbor/Daytona setup; the Snowball attempt awaits serving. Validate each additional task individually. |
| Next check | [ScienceAgentBench, bioinformatics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05080): Python analysis and scientific computing | The pinned [adapter manifest](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/96a13544537e54be84c0f316f8c3156769380684/adapters/scienceagentbench/task_manifest.json) lists 27 bioinformatics tasks: 11 Category A deterministic and 16 Category B visual. The adapter supports reference programs and task-specific numerical/file checks. | Category A needs no LLM judge; Category B defaults to GPT-4o vision. A Together replacement for Category B needs image-input and grading validation. Benchmark inputs and gold assets require a separate SharePoint download. Some tasks need GPU or additional RAM; the adapter reports CPU oracle failures. | [Adapter exists](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/96a13544537e54be84c0f316f8c3156769380684/adapters/scienceagentbench/README.md) upstream and in Marin's fork. Stage and oracle-test a CPU-suitable bioinformatics task. Include visual tasks once the vision judge is validated; selection need not be restricted to deterministic tasks. |
| Follow-up | [scBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09063): single-cell analysis from workflow snapshots | [Current release](https://github.com/latchbio/scbench/tree/0bc34032bfa402dad29fc40b4cf10ea8fc03193e) contains six example tasks with grader configurations and targets; [shared grader code](https://github.com/latchbio/latch-eval-tools) is public. All six examples use numerical tolerances; the shared library also supports label and distribution checks. | Correctness grading needs no LLM. Inputs are referenced through Latch data nodes; download/access has not been validated. Full suite is withheld. Current README describes 195 tasks/six public examples; the paper describes 394/thirty. Pin and report the actual release. | No adapter found. Follow-up port after checking data access; report a public-subset score separately from the paper's full-suite result. |
| Follow-up | [GeneBench-Pro](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/genebench-pro-public-package): judgment-heavy genomics and quantitative biology | Ten public cases include [reference_grader.py](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/genebench-pro-public-package/blob/eb75a3c0996b3cedcc9af685bad02fd166848fa2/reference_grader.py), reference answers, schemas, and tolerances. Uses numeric, integer, and exact-match checks. Boolean `passed` is authoritative; `score` is diagnostic. | Ungated public package; grader uses the Python standard library and no API key. The full 129-task suite is not contained in this release. | No adapter found. Concrete candidate for a small port: scorer checks passed below. Public cases support development and reproduction, with results reported separately from the full benchmark. |
| Follow-up | [SpatialBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.21907): spatial transcriptomics analysis | Pinned [public sample](https://github.com/latchbio/spatialbench/tree/5042c4f3ee597da1590650c7b894d068ae968e26/example_evals) contains 16 task JSONs plus a manifest. Inspected tasks include deterministic grader configurations and targets, using the shared Latch grader library. | No LLM needed for the inspected graders. Inputs use Latch data pointers; downloads remain untested. Current README describes a 159-task full suite that is withheld. | No adapter found. Candidate public-subset port after data access and selected graders are validated. |
| Follow-up | [BioAgent Bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21800v4): ten bioinformatics pipelines, including RNA-seq, variant calling, and metagenomics; corrupted-input, decoy-file, and prompt perturbations | Public [data downloader and reference pipelines](https://github.com/bioagent-bench/bioagent-bench/tree/6d098b602b8a8fdc33a9d25e410a502be7ed9ce0) and [deterministic result checks](https://github.com/bioagent-bench/bioagent-experiments/blob/35eed91676062d98d98562556ec6cce326fd7d93/tasksets/bioagent/bioagent_taskset/scoring.py) are released. Some checks accept limited overlap with reference outputs and need scientific review. | The [standard runner](https://github.com/bioagent-bench/bioagent-experiments/blob/35eed91676062d98d98562556ec6cce326fd7d93/tasksets/bioagent/bioagent_taskset/taskset.py) also calls an LLM pipeline judge. The [supplied configuration](https://github.com/bioagent-bench/bioagent-experiments/blob/35eed91676062d98d98562556ec6cce326fd7d93/configs/eval/codex.toml) uses GPT-5.4-nano through OpenRouter. Adapt and validate the Together judge route; retain deterministic result checks and LLM-assessed progress as separate metrics. | Verifiers-based standalone runner. No adapter or integration issue found in `harbor-framework/harbor` or `marin-community/harbor` on 2026-09-15. Candidate for follow-up evaluation and a Harbor port; measure data, memory, and runtime needs first. |
| Follow-up | [sc-HeurekaBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01678): open-ended single-cell scientific reasoning | [Released benchmark and evaluator](https://github.com/mlbio-epfl/HeurekaBench/tree/c2a2b2fcdc5244220ff60f65483bc084c72a8cf1/scheurekabench) include 50 open-ended and 50 multiple-choice questions. | Open-answer scoring uses an LLM judge; the paper uses GPT-4o and reports judge/human agreement checks. Configure and validate a Together judge variant and data access. The multiple-choice scoring path has not been audited. | No adapter found. Follow-up scientific-reasoning comparison; report open-answer and multiple-choice metrics separately. |
| Follow-up | [Liu et al., single-cell agent benchmark](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-026-03998-z): 50 single-cell and multi-omics tasks | Public [evaluation pipeline](https://github.com/lyyang01/bioagent-benchmark/tree/1605e6e38bd69307e2f7b68a4367de21043c89b6/evaluation) and [Zenodo data/reference analyses](https://zenodo.org/records/17291196). Combines output consistency with code, execution, and knowledge-use metrics. | The standard pipeline requires an evaluation LLM; adapt and validate its Together integration. Distinguish reference-script similarity and aggregate process metrics from biological outcome correctness. Downloads and scorer execution remain untested. | No adapter found. Diagnostic workflow evaluation. This is a separate project from BioAgent Bench above. |
| Follow-up | [BAISBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.08341): single-cell annotation and data-grounded biological discovery | Public [evaluation notebooks](https://github.com/EperLuo/BaisBench/tree/cfab1beb09a7cba999c16f01475fdca37fee5cac) cover 15 annotated datasets and 193 multiple-choice questions from 41 studies. They provide an annotation metric and reference answers. | Multiple-choice answer-key scoring offers a route without an LLM judge. Data staging, extraction of agent answers, and annotation scoring need end-to-end validation. Keep reference answers outside the agent workspace. | No adapter found. Complementary single-cell evaluation; preserve the distinction between annotation and multiple-choice discovery scores. |
| Follow-up | [BioML-bench](https://github.com/science-machine/biomlbench/tree/673f3d8d3462fc6cdcbbd9695fba612b9332ca65): biomedical ML engineering across omics, proteins, imaging, and drug discovery | [Grading code](https://github.com/science-machine/biomlbench/blob/673f3d8d3462fc6cdcbbd9695fba612b9332ca65/biomlbench/grade.py) and task-specific numerical scorers are released; inspected examples use F1 and Pearson correlation. | No LLM judge in the inspected scorers. Check each source dataset's access, reference labels, and model-fitting compute requirements. The repository identifies the release as alpha. | MLE-bench-derived standalone runner; no adapter found. Complementary ML-engineering evaluation after selecting a bounded task. |
| Follow-up | [LABBench2](https://github.com/EdisonScientific/labbench2): broad research skills, including literature, sequences, and cloning | [HybridEvaluator](https://github.com/EdisonScientific/labbench2/blob/c028ecdcf144b55ffcd92b68be45081df5628c20/evals/evaluators.py) and sequence/cloning validators are released. Dataset includes answer and validator metadata; external reference files are resolved by the runner. | HF dataset requires access acceptance. `seqqa2` and `cloning` use executable grading. Other categories use an LLM judge, defaulting to Anthropic; even `exact_match_evaluator` calls an LLM. Validate provider/model changes for the Together route. | No LABBench2 adapter found. Existing Harbor `labbench` covers original LAB-Bench FigQA. Select complementary research-skill tasks by coverage; selection need not be limited to executable grading. |
| Follow-up | [CompBioBench](https://github.com/Genentech/compbiobench-runner): 100 tasks across omics, genetics, and ML | Official hosted scorer uses whitespace-stripped exact string match. Public runner and input dataset are released; no downloadable official scorer or answer key was found. The [leaderboard code](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Genentech/compbiobench-leaderboard-v1/blob/6a63e6d2cae531d9e9bf46b341606ed6b304ba3f/app.py) delegates grading to a separate evaluator that is not publicly accessible. | Hosted submission requires Hugging Face login, answers for all 100 questions, and currently allows two submissions per user per day. No OpenAI judge key is specified. | No adapter found. Full-suite hosted scoring is available through the documented submission path. A self-contained local verifier or small-subset scorer still needs author support. |
| Follow-up: long workflows | [BixBench3](https://github.com/EdisonScientific/BixBench3): 20 research-scale analyses from raw data | [Artifact scorer](https://github.com/EdisonScientific/BixBench3/blob/d0e0bbb41222335b1b8878f533a58466a3a782dc/src/bixbench3/grading/grader.py) is released, with reference artifact packages on GCS. `bixbench3 grade` scores existing artifacts deterministically. A separate process judge evaluates the analysis trajectory. | HF dataset requires access acceptance. Artifact scoring uses no LLM; the standard cloud runner uses OpenAI for process review and web-access decisions. Validate both functions when adapting to Together. Full artifact downloads were not tested. | Standalone runner; no adapter found. Later workflow evaluation, with data and runtime costs measured explicitly. |
| Resolve assets/protocol | [BioMysteryBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Anthropic/BioMysteryBench-full): analysis of anonymized biological datasets | Reference answers and criteria are supplied in `answer_rubric`. No official executable scorer was found in the release inventory or Anthropic GitHub search. Community scorers exist, but their equivalence to Anthropic's scoring is unverified. | Full 90-task release is gated and evaluation-only; five preview tasks and their rubrics are accessible. Rubrics require both a correct answer and compliance with the source-lookup policy, so checking answer text alone is insufficient. | No adapter found. Requires a specified grading procedure, such as documented expert review for a small diagnostic pilot; automated score comparability remains unresolved. |
| Resolve assets/protocol | [BioXArena](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.15766): 76 biomedical ML tasks across nine domains | Public runner and input package; the pinned [release instructions](https://github.com/mbzuai-ai4bio/BioXArena/blob/29f88d4d573001405abf0694aee72d91c3f47e6c/README.md) state that test `answers.csv` is private. | Authors score submitted predictions against private answers. Published metrics are numerical; there is no verified self-contained local scoring route. Budget task-level model fitting separately from agent inference. | No adapter found. Requires arranging scoring and task compute before an evaluation commitment. |
| Resolve assets/protocol | [EpiBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13602): epigenomics workflow steps across accessibility, chromatin, and methylation assays | Paper describes deterministic final-answer grading. The [public release](https://github.com/latchbio/epibench/tree/6bc01f15125f5a01ab78ce1fd2fc2c51c4ca04f3/evals) contains seven task JSONs; all omit grader configurations and target answers. | A deterministic method in the paper does not supply an executable local evaluation. Inputs are Latch data pointers; data access and task-specific scorer/target access remain unresolved. Full paper suite has 106 tasks. | No adapter found. Access-dependent candidate; obtain scoring assets before porting. |
| Resolve assets/protocol | [SpatialBench-Long](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28065): study-scale spatial biological inference | Paper describes deterministic final-answer scoring and separate LLM-based trajectory rubrics. Four [public example packages](https://github.com/latchbio/spatialbench-long/tree/7de13d39ebbffee4db42675620fe0d97647e399e/evals) provide prompts/vocabularies; their task JSONs omit grader configurations and target answers. | Input access, scoring assets, and long-workflow resource budgets remain unresolved. Auxiliary LLM rubric scores must remain separate from deterministic benchmark pass/fail. | No adapter found. Later long-workflow comparison, conditional on access; public examples do not establish full-suite reproducibility. |

The literature search followed references in [BixBench](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.00096#S2), [BioAgent Bench](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21800v4#S9), and [GeneBench-Pro](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/21938268-21af-442f-af93-3b2249afb241/genebench-pro.pdf). Benchmark-specific sources and pinned release inventories are linked in the table.

Harbor availability above was checked in the adapter directories of [upstream `96a1354`](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/tree/96a13544537e54be84c0f316f8c3156769380684/adapters) and [Marin `abdd671`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/abdd67137bcd6e5c44d682d0052fbd1190e63556/adapters). Recheck open issues and pull requests before starting a port. Public task counts describe the pinned release inventories; they must not be substituted for the task counts behind published leaderboard scores.

Choose the first suite by scientific relevance, integration effort, grading availability, and measured cost. Record whether an LLM is needed for correctness grading, process review, or other runner functions.

Prioritize BixBench's existing Harbor CLI route for the first primary-suite readiness check: configure the Together judge, validate scoring on known answers, and verify that one real analysis can execute. Continue the prepared Terminal-Bench-Science smoke test to validate Snowball serving and terminal execution. ScienceAgentBench is the next integrated bioinformatics candidate; choose tasks by relevance and resource needs, with visual judging validated where used. Follow-up ports and standalone suites remain in the table. Expand to a measured pilot only after readiness checks, excluding development smoke-test tasks. The inspected `genomic-model-ranking` task specifies 2 CPUs, 4 GB RAM, no GPU, and an eight-hour agent limit; the diagnostic Snowball configuration caps the agent at 15 minutes and must be reported as a different budget.

Scorer validation: at GeneBench-Pro release `eb75a3c0996b3cedcc9af685bad02fd166848fa2`, the reference grader accepted the published reference answer for all 10 cases and rejected deliberately wrong and empty answer objects for all 10. These 30 checks ran locally without an API or analysis data. They validate the grading interface, not the scientific analyses. The documented command is `python3 reference_grader.py <eval_config.json> <eval_answer.json>`. A future adapter must expose only the task, answer schema, and analysis inputs to the agent; keep the full config, references, tolerances, reports, and grader outside its workspace.

## Status

No Snowball computational biology baseline has completed. The Terminal-Bench-Science `genomic-model-ranking` oracle completed through Harbor/Daytona on September 14 with reward 1 (Iris job `/gonzalo/bio-9160-oracle-20260914-210913`; artifacts: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/bio-9160-oracle-20260914-210913/results`). Two subsequent Snowball serving attempts ended after endpoint-readiness timeouts without obtaining GPU capacity. The expanded benchmark survey provides alternatives for evaluation coverage; no agent runs, hosted submissions, or data-access requests were made for the new candidates. The proposed October 6, 2026 target for the post-trained 67B Snowball release motivates obtaining the baseline beforehand, subject to serving availability.

First milestone:

- [ ] Select a primary benchmark and record the checkpoint, evaluation owner, serving contact, budget, and target date.
- [ ] Confirm a working endpoint or serving allocation, sandbox access, and Together judge configuration. Record the Together billing owner and pilot judge budget before paid calls. Budget serving time, sandbox task-hours, grading, setup, and retries separately.
- [ ] Pin model/tokenizer, Marin/Harbor, dataset, and container revisions. Record prompts, tools/network policy, sampling, context management, context/step/time limits, judge settings, and retry policy.
- [ ] Validate one or two development tasks: reference answers pass, deliberately wrong answers fail, missing submissions are accounted for, and a real analysis can execute. Keep reference answers, solutions, and verifier material inaccessible to the solving agent. The BixBench oracle writes an answer directly, so it checks grading without reproducing the analysis.
- [ ] Run one prespecified task once and measure serving time, sandbox time, and grading cost. Expand to 5–10 prespecified tasks only after checking the measured cost against the pilot budget; retain the first task in that pilot. Exclude the development smoke-test tasks from the measured pilot. For BixBench, select questions from distinct data capsules (separate source notebooks and their associated data) and record their IDs before examining their Snowball results.
- [ ] Publish configs, trajectories, produced artifacts, success counts, coverage, runtime/cost, and a short failure analysis. Report successes over all scheduled attempts and over attempts with a determined model outcome. Coverage is the fraction of scheduled attempts with a determined model outcome. Count agent-caused missing submissions and timeouts as failures unless a retained verifier result establishes success. Exclude unresolved infrastructure and grader errors only from the second denominator; report their counts and coverage separately.
- [ ] Decide whether to expand the primary suite, repair the harness, or validate a second benchmark. Record the evidence and follow-up owner.

For subsequent checkpoint comparisons, hold the task set, harness, and execution budget fixed. Keep inspected development tasks separate from an untouched final evaluation set. Preserve each baseline and record protocol changes. Evaluation-only materials and inspected evaluation trajectories must stay out of training.

Treat all ten public GeneBench-Pro cases as development and reproduction material for this effort. Any final set whose results have not guided model or protocol changes must be selected separately before follow-on training; the initial pilot does not supply that final set.

Count each fresh agent rollout, including retries, as a separate attempt and report first-attempt success separately. Regrading an existing submission does not create a new agent attempt.

## Links

- Planning context: [Bio-Snowball proposal](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1UnoAHNlkRAskxC9fAnF1SMpiU4QnFg-A8x9aXoEQ_MI/edit?tab=t.x53y2cvqravy).
- Starting assets: [Snowball SFT and evaluations, #8225](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8225), [archived serving and agent configurations](https://gist.github.com/penfever/34e22b004327aa220ccdcfc87b29a0ec/cfeaa1ad862586676f4de189cc2e8bcf067ea2f5).
- Evaluation integration: [launcher documentation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evaluation/README.md), [evaluation architecture discussion, #7345](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7345).
- Benchmark discovery: [Harbor Hub](https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets?scope=all), [upstream adapters](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/tree/main/adapters), [Marin's Harbor fork](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/main/adapters).
- Run artifacts and reports: add as runs complete; keep raw logs and dense results in the artifact store.

## Decision Log

2026-09-14: Plan the pilot without requiring a personal OpenAI API key. Make BixBench conditional on project-provided judge access, which has not been arranged, and prioritize a readiness check of an existing Harbor-native task with executable grading. The primary suite and execution budget remain unconfirmed.

2026-09-14 scorer audit: distinguish CompBioBench's documented full-suite hosted scoring from its unavailable local scorer. Add GeneBench-Pro's public cases as a concrete porting option after 30 successful scorer checks. No agent runs, hosted submissions, or gated-data access requests were made in this audit.

2026-09-15: Add BioAgent Bench as a candidate for pipeline execution and robustness evaluation. The [v4 paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21800v4) reports GPT-5.1-judged pipeline completion; the current runner separates deterministic `results_match` from LLM-assessed progress. Report these metrics separately, and identify any evaluation using only deterministic checks as a distinct protocol. Validate reference and deliberately wrong outputs before selecting tasks. The paper targets workflows under four hours and within 48 GB RAM; these are design constraints, not measured pilot costs. This addition is based on source inspection; no BioAgent task or scorer has been run in this effort.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Canonical evaluation model configs expose tensor and data parallelism, but not pipeline parallelism. This prevents the blessed `experiments.evaluation.cli launch` path from serving an evaluation model across multiple Iris tasks.

The immediate failure is [GLM-5.2 AWQ INT4 on TB2.1](https://evaldash.oa.dev/runs/20260813-011602-glm-5.2-awq-int4-glm-5.2-awq-int4-tb21-aa-7bc9). At `max_model_len: 1048576`, TP8 on one H100x8 node loaded 62.35 GiB of weights per rank, then vLLM failed before any trial ran:

```
ValueError: No available memory for the cache blocks. Try increasing `gpu_memory_utilization`
```

PP2 with TP8 inside each node would reduce stage-local weight memory while retaining NVLink for tensor parallelism. Marin already has Iris gang rendezvous and native vLLM PP support from #7758. That implementation is currently exercised as PP2/TP1/DP8 for Grug; its helper fixes local TP to 1, and the evaluation path does not call it.

The remaining gaps are visible in [`ServeConfig`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/66487ec75071fe96d04459aabfab8cf806c905f2/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/model_config.py#L63-L89), [GPU topology validation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/66487ec75071fe96d04459aabfab8cf806c905f2/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/hardware.py#L170-L180), and [evaluation serving lowering](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/66487ec75071fe96d04459aabfab8cf806c905f2/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/serving_config.py#L258-L278). They model one GPU slice and validate only `TP × DP`.

Done when:

- Evaluation model YAML can declare pipeline parallelism separately from per-node tensor and data parallelism.
- The launcher validates per-node GPU use and total gang geometry.
- PP2/TP8 lowers to two coscheduled H100x8 Iris tasks and starts one distributed vLLM endpoint.
- Dry-run output and durable evaluation records preserve the resolved PP, TP, DP, task count, and per-task accelerator shape.
- A behavioral test covers a multi-node evaluation topology and rejects inconsistent geometry before submission.

Tracked from #8083.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Launching `experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/swebench-recovery.yaml`, whose dataset is `name: hf://DCAgent2/swebench-verified-random-100-folders`, now fails in the launcher's Harbor preflight before anything is submitted:

```
Error: Invalid value for --evalchemy-config/--harbor-config: invalid Harbor config in [.../swebench-recovery.yaml]:
[{"type":"value_error","loc":["name"],"msg":"Value error, Package name must be in 'org/name' format with alphanumeric characters, hyphens, underscores, and dots. Cannot start with a dot or contain '..'. Got: hf://DCAgent2/swebench-verified-random-100-folders", ...}]
```

`datasets[].name: hf://org/repo` is a Marin convention (`experiments/evaluation/README.md`, `_HF_DATASET_PREFIX` in `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/trial_driver.py`); Harbor itself never accepts it, and its `PackageReference` validator is unchanged between the 9551f376 and abdd6713 pins. Before #9145 (b9ccaa6) the preflight in `trial_driver.py` substituted `_PLACEHOLDER_DATASET_PATH` for every non-registry dataset, so Harbor validated a path and never saw the `hf://` name. #9145 replaced that with `dataset_path = ... if dataset_metadata.kind == _DatasetKind.LOCAL else None` and calls `Job.create(effective)` to publish benchmark metadata, so a Hugging Face dataset reaches Harbor's `is_package()` check with its raw `hf://` name and is rejected. The same config launched at Marin 6bc19cb. The other four cohort Harbor policies use registry datasets and validate.

Reproduce:
1. `uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch --model-config <any GPU catalog yaml> --harbor-config experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/swebench-recovery.yaml --federated_cluster cw-rno2a --priority interactive --version test --dry-run`
2. The command exits with the validation error above.

Expected: the preflight materializes or masks `hf://` datasets the way the trial driver does at run time, so Hugging Face-backed Harbor policies validate and report their benchmark metadata. Observed on the eval-policy release branch 97dd188d5e (`main` plus two eval commits).

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 @karansag, flagging this one for you since #9145 introduced the regression. The eval-policy release branch carries a fix as marin-community/marin@7984ab94683e87cde65ec0adb47f0a235ffec9b6 (`benfeuer/bump-evalchemy-sandbox-fix`): the preflight downloads the `hf://` snapshot into the Hugging Face cache and hands Harbor the copied task tree, so `swebench-recovery.yaml` validates and reports `n_benchmark=100`. A cold preflight takes about 13s. The same change forwards `HF_TOKEN` to the driver. `tests/evaluation/test_harbor_trial_driver.py::test_preflight_materializes_hugging_face_datasets` covers it.

Two things worth knowing when landing this on `main`: the module-scoped `checked_policies` fixture in that test file preflights all 17 policies, several of them `hf://` datasets, so on `main` it has been failing since #9145 for the same reason; with the fix it runs but the 739-file bfcl-parity download hits the unauthenticated Hugging Face rate limit unless `HF_TOKEN` is set. And `ds-1000-local.yaml` fails its preflight because `experiments/evaluation/local_datasets/ds1000` is absent from the checkout.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
`build_model_args` in `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/client.py:72` sends `tokenizer=<checkpoint>,tokenizer_backend=huggingface` on every lm-eval route and never passes `trust_remote_code`. On the chat route the endpoint applies the chat template, so the client tokenizer is unused, but lm-eval still loads it at model init. Two cohort models fail every Evalchemy eval at that step, on Evalchemy 07c7cce as well as the older pin:

- google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it: `Failed to initialize model: 'list' object has no attribute 'keys'` (Gemma 4 tokenizer metadata against the client's Transformers 4).
- moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct: `Failed to initialize model: The repository ... contains custom code which must be executed to correctly load the model`.

marin-community/evalchemy#140 fixed both in Evalchemy's own serve-eval runner (`tokenizer_backend=none` for chat, `trust_remote_code=True` for completions), but Marin's eval child calls the `evalchemy` CLI with its own argument string, so the fix never reaches Marin launches. Eval configs cannot work around it: `tokenizer_backend` is in `RESERVED_ENDPOINT_MODEL_ARGS`, so `extra_model_args` may not override it.

Reproduce:
1. `uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch --model-config <catalog yaml for google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it> --evals math500 --federated_cluster cw-rno2a --priority interactive --version test`
2. The `eval-math500-*` child exits 1 with `Failed to initialize model: 'list' object has no attribute 'keys'`.

Expected: chat-route launches send `tokenizer_backend=none` and no `tokenizer`; completion-route launches keep the local tokenizer for loglikelihood scoring and pass `trust_remote_code=True`. Both models then evaluate.

Fix applied on the eval-policy release branch as marin-community/marin@97dd188d5e (`benfeuer/bump-evalchemy-sandbox-fix`), with a test in `tests/evals/test_evalchemy_config.py`; it needs to land on `main`.

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
Status: proposed. The generation recipe, first task family, and pilot size remain to be selected.

Generate synthetic training data for computational biology, starting with task families covered by designated in-distribution (ID) biology evaluations. Produce executable Harbor tasks and teacher trajectories with per-attempt rewards for supervised fine-tuning (SFT), with validated tasks also available for later reinforcement learning (RL).

The initial question is whether we can generate biologically meaningful, solvable tasks with reliable graders at a useful cost. Effects on model performance would require a subsequent training experiment.

Scope:

- Generate new tasks that exercise skills represented in the selected ID evaluations, with fresh inputs and independently established expected results. Candidate sources include biological datasets, analysis workflows, and bioinformatics repositories.
- Follow [Marin's evaluation policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9193): exclude out-of-distribution evaluations from task design, deduplicate against evaluation data, and keep teacher rollouts on evaluation questions out of training. ID evaluation instructions must not be used directly as RL data.
- Keep the implementation in `marin-community/marin` on an experimental branch, provisionally under `experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/`. A merge to `main` is not a prerequisite for this experiment. Record the code revision and any local changes used for each run.

Candidate approaches:

1. Generate tasks from a description of an ID task family, specifying new data, an analysis objective, expected outputs, and a verifier. For example, construct a differential-expression analysis task over a different dataset and compute reference outputs independently.
2. Derive tasks from biological code or workflows through instruction backtranslation, or adapt a repository-based generation recipe such as [SWE-smith](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-smith) or [SERA](https://github.com/allenai/SERA). Packaging these tasks for Harbor and establishing a trustworthy grader are separate steps.

Start with one approach and one task family. GLM-5.3 is a candidate teacher; record the model identity and generation settings actually used. Reuse Marin's existing launch and rollout machinery where applicable, and preserve Marin's evaluation defaults for benchmark comparisons.

Existing work to reuse:

- [Scientific-repository backtranslation (#7813)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7813): related Marin work covering bioinformatics repositories. The issue names uncommitted implementation files that were absent from `main` when inspected; locate the working branch before planning to reuse them.
- [OpenThoughts-Agent self-instruct](https://github.com/open-thoughts/OpenThoughts-Agent/tree/main/data/self_instruct): task generation from source text, with separate verifier-authoring code. Adapt useful components after inspecting their behavior and dependencies, preserving applicable licenses and attribution.
- [Marin's TaskTrove pipeline](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/main/experiments/post_training/tasktrove): an existing pattern for converting, validating, deduplicating, and recording the provenance of Harbor tasks.

Pilot work:

- [ ] Select the ID task family and source material; document what the generated tasks should test.
- [ ] Generate Harbor tasks containing instructions, input data, an environment, a reference solution, and a verifier. Keep reference answers unavailable to the solving agent.
- [ ] Review a sample for biological validity and instruction clarity. Check that reference solutions pass and deliberately incorrect or empty outputs fail; record rejected tasks and reasons.
- [ ] Check for overlap with evaluation data and duplicates within the generated set. Retain source identifiers and generation provenance.
- [ ] Collect teacher attempts on accepted synthetic tasks. Retain traces, rewards, model failures, and infrastructure failures before applying any SFT selection rule.
- [ ] Report accepted and rejected task counts, verifier defects, teacher success rates, token usage, runtime, and estimated cost. Record limitations and negative results alongside the artifacts.

The pilot is complete when its task dataset and reward-bearing trajectories can be inspected and reproduced, with a documented decision to expand, revise, or stop the recipe. A useful negative result also completes the pilot. Any claim of improved biology capability requires a training comparison under a fixed evaluation protocol.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Public reproduction inputs for the Snowball 67B-A2B RLVR1 sync and async arms on Iris cw-rno2a are available. The package has two canonical configs and one typed launcher. Both launch modes passed trainer/Hydra/Iris dry runs at their pinned MarinSkyRL commits; no reproduction GPU job was submitted.

## Description

The comparison covers sync v65 and the async v108 → v110 → v113 line. Both use the September 11 step-159000 SFT model, an ordered 84,426-row RLVR1 training set, 32,768-token request windows, and eight 8×H100 nodes per job. The async config has TIS, router replay, full TITO, and maximum staleness 2. Its 89-row holdout excludes 11 LiveCodeBench/code-generation rows; the sync holdout has 100 rows.

## Timing interpretation correction (2026-09-18)

The sync v65 and async v108/v110/v113 configs both use TP1/PP2/CP2/EP8 for policy and reference, with sample packing disabled. The sync v65 launch script explicitly sets CP2/EP8. A timing report incorrectly described that sync arm as packed TP1/PP2/CP1/EP16; that description has been corrected. The recorded step times are unchanged, but geometry and packing are not differences between these arms and cannot explain the timing gap. The trainer paths, async features, response lengths, and validation sets still differ.

## Hypothesis / goal

Make the exact launch choices and consumed data independently inspectable, and make fresh sync/async runs reproducible on Iris cw-rno2a without copying checkpoints into the public package.

## Status and links

- [Public data and provenance, pinned revision](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-RLVR1-Repro-Data/tree/5af04cf16ec7773487e5a7663933ee515de1cfa4): train/validation Parquet, hashes, filtering record, and mixed-license source attribution.
- [Public reproduction gist](https://gist.github.com/penfever/28284d13f0092fb8859307fe96d5529b): `sync.yaml`, `async.yaml`, `launch.py`, launch instructions, source/runtime pins, campaign policy, and checksum verifier.
- [Pinned starting SFT model](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.11/tree/50a201b16de975505e981a9e186b1f8aa5f53c91).
- MarinSkyRL source: [sync `5666cbb`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/commit/5666cbbb25b5ce92d9f4ce2c290dbef6fc6628ca), [async `e480b4d`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/commit/e480b4dd274272ba573ca8743a8128f85e3b4785). Task and uploader image digests are pinned in the gist README.

Use the gist README to prepare clean pinned worktrees and dry-run `launch.py sync` or `launch.py async`. Download the published Parquet files and stage them in Iris S3 if the original input URIs are unavailable; pass `--train-data-uri` and `--val-data-uri` to the launcher. Add `--submit` only when the dry run and output paths have been reviewed. The launcher submits via the historical Marin/Iris CPU-coordinator path targeting cw-rno2a and requires the usual Iris, sandbox, and Together credentials.

## Decision log

- 2026-09-18: Kept only two effective launch records and one launcher; retained the exact original source/runtime pins and input hashes.
- 2026-09-18: Published data separately from lightweight launch artifacts. No checkpoint or model weights were copied.
- 2026-09-18: Dry-ran fresh sync, fresh async, and staged-data URI overrides. Did not submit a GPU job.

## Reproducibility limits

The public inputs support a **fresh** sync or async run from the SFT model. Replaying the exact v113 continuation requires the private v108 `global_step_18` checkpoint via `--resume-from`; it is intentionally not included. The historical Marin/Iris control-plane revision and earlier v108/v110 pod image IDs were not retained. Judge responses, scheduling, and async ordering are nondeterministic, so bitwise replay is not claimed.

The trainer paths, async features, response lengths, and validation sets differ, so this is not an isolated async-algorithm measurement. The issue body and timing report have been corrected. issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
Track biology evaluation coverage, tooling, and results for reference models and Snowball. This includes selecting benchmarks, defining comparable protocols, supporting their execution in Marin, and following results across models and checkpoints. The initial evaluation paths are non-agentic questions through Evalchemy and agentic biological analysis through Harbor.

Use Marin's existing protocols where available. Report question-answering and agentic-task results separately, with explicit task coverage and aggregation rules. Keep evaluation items isolated from training data.

Work to track:

- [ ] Select biology benchmarks and document the capabilities each measures, its limitations, and gaps in overall coverage. MMLU biology is the starting selection; additional non-agentic benchmarks remain to be chosen.
- [ ] Establish the first Harbor-based biology evaluation, recording the benchmark variant, agent harness, and grading protocol. BixBench is a candidate; benchmark and grader choices remain to be finalized.
- [ ] Address integration gaps for selected benchmarks, including reusable configurations, launchers, scoring, and Eval Dash visibility.
- [ ] Evaluate reference models and Snowball checkpoints under comparable protocols.
- [ ] Track results with model identity, task and evaluator revisions, per-task scores, coverage, failures, and aggregation rules so comparisons remain interpretable.
- [x] Complete the first GLM-5.3 MMLU biology evaluation and verify scores, full coverage, and Eval Dash ingestion.
- [x] Publish the initial biology-task configuration and runner on a branch, with code permalinks.

First completed evaluation:

GLM-5.3 was evaluated on three MMLU subjects on September 18, 2026. `MMLU-biology` names this selection: `mmlu_college_biology`, `mmlu_high_school_biology`, and `mmlu_medical_genetics`.

| Subject | Correct / questions | Accuracy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| College biology | 117 / 144 | 81.25% |
| High-school biology | 267 / 310 | 86.13% |
| Medical genetics | 78 / 100 | 78.00% |

All 554 questions were evaluated using Marin's five-shot answer-choice likelihood protocol, seed 42, and no item cap. The existing Eval Dash aggregate is **81.79%**, averaging the three subject accuracies equally. Accuracy across individual questions is **83.39% (462/554)**. No unanswered items or infrastructure errors were recorded; an audit of the native outputs reproduced every grade. [EvalDash run — Marina access required](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/glm53-mmlu-biology-full-20260918-191647).

Public code references:

- [Biology task configuration](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a28c29a008a3ddc1a62fb348c52217a4429e5491/experiments/evaluation/configs/evalchemy/mmlu-biology.yaml).
- [GLM-5.3 runner adapted from the completed evaluation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a28c29a008a3ddc1a62fb348c52217a4429e5491/experiments/evaluation/glm53_mmlu_biology.py).
- [Integration changes and usage documentation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/a28c29a008a3ddc1a62fb348c52217a4429e5491).
- [Marin MMLU configuration at the run's base revision](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3071922e5d29f3dd0f924ca0881d71fbe5c7fca9/experiments/evaluation/configs/evalchemy/mmlu.yaml#L1-L6).
- [Marin's Evalchemy configuration builder at the same revision](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3071922e5d29f3dd0f924ca0881d71fbe5c7fca9/experiments/evaluation/evals.py#L197-L244).
- [Pinned Evalchemy revision used for the evaluation](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/commit/412ae9c29c0f261581181f8668dc316a2144f0c7).

The reusable runner is an adaptation of the completed experiment; its commit is not the original run’s source revision. The exact model weights revision was unavailable, and the dataset revision followed the evaluator defaults; those limitations should accompany comparisons with future runs.

comments.body:
🤖 BixBench CLI development check: the explicit 10 GiB retry ran through the agent phase, but produced no scored answer. The initial attempt had been blocked before model inference because the task's default 20 GB disk request exceeded the Daytona account's 10 GB per-sandbox cap.

The retry used `environment.override_storage_mb: 10240`, following a [previous Harbor canary that hit the same limit](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/75#issuecomment-5461786985). Development outcome:

- Sandbox setup completed. The agent ran for its original 3,600-second budget without creating `/workspace/answer.txt`.
- BixBench's unchanged verifier returns without writing a reward when the answer file is missing. Harbor recorded `RewardFileNotFoundError`; no Together judge decision was produced. The canonical record reports **1 attempted, 0 scored**. This is not a judged incorrect answer or a benchmark accuracy estimate.
- The end-of-agent filesystem diagnostic reported **25.7 MiB used and 9.97 GiB available** in the 10 GiB allocation. No disk-exhaustion failure was observed. This is a final filesystem reading, not peak usage or the base image's total size, and it does not establish that every capsule fits.

Protocol:

- CLI adaptation, registry `bixbench-cli@1.5`, [task revision `711ff277`](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-datasets/tree/711ff277ae6b9e3950d19b40bc3e5aeb96e62b73/datasets/bixbench-cli). One development task, `bix-1-q1`, excluded from the subsequent five-question pilot. The complete registry snapshot has 205 questions.
- GLM-5.3 with Terminus-2; Harbor [`7b18505a`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/7b18505a56e5624f55887e3b20f4de452f698a7a) and its dependency lockfile. Use the [September evaluation policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9193): 32,768 input tokens, 8,192 output tokens, and the default enabled summarization.
- Together `openai/gpt-oss-120b` verifier with BixBench's original grading prompt and Boolean response schema. Four basic live checks passed: exact and equivalent numeric answers accepted; wrong and empty answers rejected. This checks grader integration, not broad judge accuracy.
- The original base image is ARM-only. Use the [adapter author's AMD64 replacement](https://github.com/Future-House/BixBench/issues/41#issuecomment-4340332343), pinned to `sha256:485e5c776422fece8cb98addba593ea188c8a97162807a91d2a0e350522407b7`, with capsule data pinned to Hugging Face revision `f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a`.

The five-question pilot has not been launched. Before expanding, review the no-answer timeout behavior and complete a native verifier check that reaches the judge. The current failure remains in the record; it must not disappear from attempted coverage. This exploratory CLI protocol should be reported separately from the original notebook-based BixBench leaderboard and from Marin's canonical benchmark suite.

comments.body: 🤖 Correction after tracing the current checkpoint path: the long-lived `GlobalAsyncCheckpointManager` keeps the completed TensorStore commit futures in `_commit_futures`; `wait_until_finished()` joins but does not clear them, and the writes allow indefinite source-buffer references. spillover_issues.author: dlwh
spillover_issues.body:
Parent tracker: #6693

Owner: matt

## Description
Prototype and evaluate FP8 Expert GMM path with a baseline against bf16 expert GMM.

### Definition of Done
- Reproducible command/branch for FP8 run path exists.
- Report timing and MFU delta vs bf16 baseline (target >=40% speedup).
- Include numerical/stability checks and memory usage notes.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Analysis (not a PR):** This is a research/prototyping + benchmarking task (reproducible FP8 run path, MFU/timing/memory measurement on TPU, ≥40% speedup target). Per the agent workflow it's out of scope for an auto-PR — posting root-cause/code map and a proposed approach for a human (matt) to drive.

# Research

FP8 quant exists (`Fp8DotGeneralOp`, `quantize_linear_layers`) and is wired into the dense `Linear` layer via its `dot_general` field, but the MoE expert path runs through `ragged_dot` (grouped matmul / megablox on TPU) which has **no** quantization hook — `MoELinear` explicitly leaves it as a TODO. So an FP8 expert GMM path does not exist today and must be built where `ragged_dot` is called.

**Relevant code**
- [`linear.py#L194-L200`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/haliax/src/haliax/nn/linear.py#L194-L200) — `MoELinear` with `# TODO: support quantization for ragged_dot?` (no `dot_general` field)
- [`linear.py#L233-L310`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/haliax/src/haliax/nn/linear.py#L233-L310) — `MoELinear.__call__` / `_gmm`, the expert matmul call sites
- [`ragged_dot.py#L67-L392`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/haliax/src/haliax/nn/ragged_dot.py#L67-L392) — `ragged_dot()` + megablox/Triton/XLA backends (the GMM to quantize)
- [`fp8.py#L122-L150`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/haliax/src/haliax/_src/fp8.py#L122-L150) — `dot_general_with_precision`, the FP8 QDQ matmul primitive to reuse
- [`quantization.py#L154-L256`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/haliax/src/haliax/quantization.py#L154-L256) — `Fp8DotGeneralOp`, `QuantizationConfig`, `quantize_linear_layers`

# Proposed Approach

Minimal prototype → benchmark, in three steps:

1. **Add an FP8 GMM path.** Introduce a quantized variant alongside `ragged_dot` plumbed to per-group e4m3fn QDQ of activations + expert weights, reusing the QDQ machinery in `fp8.py`. On TPU the megablox `gmm` accepts low-precision operands directly; start there and keep the XLA path as a numeric reference. Gate it behind a config flag on `MoEExpertMlp` (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py`) / `MoELinear` rather than the dense-`Linear` `Fp8DotGeneralOp` (which doesn't cover ragged_dot).
2. **Reproducible run path.** Wire the flag through the MoE config so a single config toggles bf16↔fp8 for a known model (Mixtral / Qwen3-MoE / grug MoE). Record the exact branch + launch command in this issue.
3. **Measure** on one TPU config: forward+backward timing and MFU bf16 vs fp8 (target ≥40%), peak HBM, and a numerical/stability check (cosine sim / max-abs-err of expert outputs and grads, plus a short loss-curve sanity run) — fp8 e4m3 for fwd, consider e5m2 for grads.

Open questions for matt before implementation: (a) which model/scale is the baseline; (b) TPU generation (v5e/v6e — affects whether megablox fp8 is supported in the pinned JAX); (c) scope to forward-only fp8 first, or fwd+bwd. Happy to implement step 1 as a scoped PR once the target model/hardware is fixed.
